q_en: What is the solid crust or the hard top layer of the earth called?
e_en: The correct answer is option D) i.e. Lithosphere. The lithosphere is a rigid, rocky outer layer of the Earth, consisting of the crust and the solid outermost layer of the upper mantle. It extends to a depth of about 100 km. It comprises the rocks of the earth’s crust and the thin layers of soil that contain nutrient elements that sustain organisms. There are two main divisions of the earth’s surface.

q_en: Dogri language is mainly spoken in which of the following states/union territories?
e_en: The correct answer is option D) i.e. Jammu and Kashmir. Dogri language, member of the Indo-Aryan group within the Indo-European languages. The earliest written reference to Dogri is found in the Nuh sipihr (“The Nine Heavens”), written by the poet Amir Khusru in 1317 CE.

q_en: The first defence minister of independent India was:
e_en: The correct answer is option A) i.e. Baldev Singh. Baldev Singh (1902-1961) was the first Defence Minister of India at Independence. He was also an Industrialist and Politician. He died in 1961.

q_en: Who was the first Indian to cross the English Channel?
e_en: The correct answer is option A) i.e. Mihir Sen. Mihir Sen is the first Indian and also the first Asian to cross the English Channel. He achieved this feat on September 27 in the year 1958. The English Channel is a part of the Atlantic Ocean that divides the island of Great Britain from Northern France. The channel has a length of 563 km and a width of 240 km.

q_en: Who among the following is the longest serving President of India?
e_en: The correct answer is option A) i.e. Rajendra Prasad. Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the first president of India. He is also the longest serving president of India from 1950-62. A lawyer by profession, Dr. Prasad was an influential leader during the Indian freedom struggle. He served as the president of the Constituent Assembly that drafted the first constitution of the Republic of India, which lasted from 1948 to 1950.

tribals whose customary rights were being violated

q_en: One-third of the members of the Vidhan Parishad retire every ______ year/s.
e_en: The correct answer is two. Vidhan Parishad or the State Legislative Council is the upper house in those states that have a bicameral legislature. q_en: Who among the following travellers came to India from Uzbekistan in the 11th century?

q_en: Which of the following crops is grown throughout the year in the southern states of India?

Rice growing in India varies for different parts of the country based on the varying altitude and climate. Factors of growth: Temperature, rainfall, soil types, water availability. Since a mean temperature is found in the eastern and western regions which are favourable for rice cultivation it is grown throughout the year.

q_en: LAC (Line of Actual Control) is an effective border between India and ______.
e_en: The correct answer is China. The LAC (Line of Actual Control) is the demarcation that separates Indian-controlled territory from Chinese-controlled territory. q_en: Which one of the following is the largest valley in Asia?

Charles Elton was an English ecologist who first described the characteristic shape of ecological trophic interactions which he called the pyramid of numbers. Elton observed that most food webs have many organisms on their bottom trophic levels and successively fewer on the subsequent, higher levels. A food web is the natural interconnection of food chains and a graphical representation of what eats what in an ecological community.

e_en: The correct answer is Anita Desai. Fasting, Feasting is a novel by Indian writer Anita Desai, first published in 1999 in Great Britain by Chatto & Windus. It was shortlisted for the Booker Prize for fiction in 1999. This novel of intricate family relations plays out in two countries, India and the United States. The story focuses on the life of the unmarried and main character, Uma, a spinster, the family's older daughter, with Arun, the boy and baby of the family.

q_en: On the basis of the track width of Indian Railways, what type of gauge is Matheran Hill Railways?
e_en: The correct answer is Narrow gauge. The small gauge is called a Narrow gauge or a small line. The narrow-gauge railway is the railway track, in which the distance between two tracks is 2 ft 6 in (762 mm) and 2 ft (610 mm). In 2015, there was a 1,500 km narrow gauge rail route, which is considered to be about 2% of the total Indian rail network. In 2015, Now the small lines are being converted into big lines. Trains with small bogies now will no longer be able to see much.

q_en: A R Rahman, the famous musician won the 52nd Grammy Award for which of the following songs?
e_en: The correct answer is Jai Ho. Allah Rakha Rahman is an Indian film composer, record producer, singer, and, songwriter who works predominantly in Indian cinema. Rahman is now a Golden Globe® winner for "Best Original Soundtrack" for SLUMDOG MILLIONAIRE and has been nominated for three Oscars for the film, for best original score and two for best original songs. In 2010, the Indian government awarded him the Padma Bhushan, the nation's third-highest civilian award.

q_en: Which plateau, with an average elevation of about 600 meters (2000 feet), is bounded by three mountain ranges: the Satpura range to the north and the Eastern and Western Ghats on either side?
e_en: The correct answer is Deccan Plateau. The large Deccan Plateau in southern India is located between the Western Ghats and the Eastern Ghats. It is loosely defined as the peninsular region between these ranges that is south of the Narmada river. To the north, it is bounded by the Satpura and Vindhya Ranges. The plateau is drier than the coastal region of India. It ranges between 100 and 1,000 meters (330 and 3,280 ft), with an average elevation of about 600 meters (2,000 ft).

q_en:
Lack of financial discipline by the government can lead to ______.
(A) excess expenditure
(B) inflation
e_en: The correct answer is A and B. Financial discipline is the act of setting specific monetary (spending and saving) goals and measuring oneself against how well they are achieved. Once that financial discipline is established, a person can take further steps to become financially pendent. Excessive expenditure means the portion of expenditure incurred that significantly exceeds the amounts normally charged for treatment in the country where the treatment was provided.

q_en: Pandit Bhawani Shankar is a ______ player.
e_en: The correct answer is pakhawaj. ​Bhawani Shankar is a renowned Indian classical percussionist. He began playing the Pakhawaj and tabla under the guidance of his father, Pandit Babulalji, a recognised maestro of Kathak dance, pakhawaj and tabla from the Jaipur Gharana.

q_en: Which cricket player’s autobiography is titled ‘281 and Beyond’?
e_en: The correct answer is VVS Laxman. A stylish batsman who could score against any kind of bowling, VVS Laxman played over a hundred Tests to aggregate more than 8,000 runs. Cricket fans still remember with awe his game-changing knock of 281 against Australia in 2001 at Eden Gardens. Vangipurapu Venkata Sai Laxman is a former Indian international cricketer and a former cricket commentator and pundit.

q_en: Which of the following is the oldest High Court?
e_en: The correct answer is Calcutta High Court. The Calcutta High Court is the oldest High Court in India. It is located in B.B.D. Bagh, Kolkata, West Bengal. It has jurisdiction over the state of West Bengal and the Union Territory of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. The High Court building's design is based on the Cloth Hall, Ypres, in Belgium. The high court was established on 1 July 1862. The current chief justice of Calcutta High Court is Justice T. S. Sivagnanam.

q_en: Maitya Ram Reang (Satyaram) was conferred with the Padma Shri for his contributions to which of the folk dances?
e_en: The correct answer is Hojagiri. Hojagiri is a folk dance, performed in the state of Tripura, India by the Tripuri people of the Reang clan. It is performed by women and young girls, about 4 to 6 members in a team, singing, balancing on an earthen pitcher, and managing other props such as a bottle on the head and an earthen lamp on the hand. Satyaram Reang is an Indian folk performer and folk artist from Tripura. He is noted for his significant contribution to Hojagiri Dance.

q_en: Which is the first of India's traditional dance to be refashioned as a theatre art and to be exhibited widely both at home and abroad?
e_en: The correct answer is Bharatanatyam. Bharatanatyam is a major form of Indian classical dance that originated in Tamil Nadu. The Natya Shastra by Bharata Muni and Abhinaya Darpana by Nandikeshvara are considered to be the original sources of Bharatanatyam. The dance form is also briefly mentioned in the Kannada text Manasollasa written by Someshwara III. Lord Shiva is considered the god of this dance form.

q_en: Which organisation was created in 1988 by the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) and the United Nations Environment Program (UNEP) to assess the science related to climate change ?
e_en: The correct answer is Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC). The river originates in the Nandi Hills in the Chikkaballapura district of Karnataka and flows through Tamil Nadu before emptying into the Bay of Bengal.

q_en: Who among the following has written the Hindi novel 'Kafan'?

q_en: When the government resorts to borrowing only to clear the backlog of interest payments, it is referred to as __________.

It is not adding to the existing loans for any purpose other than meeting its existing obligations of interest payment. It is a sign of fiscal discipline or fiscal responsibility on the part of the government.

3 : 19 :: 2 : 7 :: 5 : ?
e_en: Logic : Cube of first number - Cube of (first number - 1) = Second number 3 : 19 ⇒ 3³ - (3 - 1)³ ⇒ 3³ - 2³ = 19 2 : 7 ⇒ 2³ - (2 - 1)³ ⇒ 2³ - 1³ = 7 Similarly, 5 : ? ⇒ 5³ - (5 - 1)³ ⇒ 5³ - 4³ = 61 Hence, 61 is the correct answer.

Ten states currently have Fifth Schedule Areas: Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Rajasthan, and Telangana.

In 1972, the United Nations General Assembly established World Environment Day on the first day of the Stockholm Conference on the Human Environment.

Himadri is also known as Inner Himalayas or Greater Himalayas. Himachal is also known as Middle Himalayas or Lesser Himalayas. Shiwalik is also known as Outer Himalayas.

q_en: What is the average height of inner Himalayas?

Consider the given consumption function of country X and answer the following question.
C = 100 + 0.8Y
What is the value of autonomous consumption (A) and marginal propensity to consume (MPC) in the given equation?
e_en: Correct Answer A = 100, MPC = 0.8 The consumption function you provided is in the form of a simple linear equation: C = A + MPC*Y where: C represents consumption, A represents autonomous consumption, MPC represents the marginal propensity to consume, and Y represents income. Comparing this with your given function C = 100 + 0.8Y, we can identify the values of A and MPC. A (Autonomous consumption) is part of consumption that occurs when income is zero.

q_en: Which among the following is India's first corporatized port?
e_en: The correct answer is Ennore. q_en: The collection of all bundles that the consumer can buy with her income at the prevailing market prices is called the _____.
e_en: The correct answer is Budget set. The collection of all bundles that the consumer can buy with her income at the prevailing market prices is called the Budget set. The budget set represents all the combinations of goods and services that the consumer can afford given the prices and their income. This set is subject to the budget constraint, which is the limitation on the consumer's income that they cannot surpass.

q_en: Where is the World Heritage Site, Konark Sun Temple situated in India?
e_en: The correct answer is Odisha. The Konark Sun Temple is a 13th-century Hindu temple dedicated to the sun god Surya. It is located in Konark, a town in the Puri district of Odisha, India. Sun Temple of Konark was built by King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga Dynasty about 1250 CE. This temple is dedicated to the Hindu god Surya and located 35 km northeast from Puri.

q_en: Where does Alaknanda River join Bhagirathi River in India?

Devprayag is considered one of the Panch Prayag (five confluences) in Uttarakhand, which holds immense religious significance for Hindus.

q_en: Indian Standard Time (IST) is ahead of Greenwich Mean Time (GMT) by ______.

The city of Mirzapur, Uttar Pradesh, is situated on the longitude reference line of 82.5°E, making it the reference point for calculating Indian Standard Time.

q_en: Who was the first Indian woman to be appointed Chief Justice of a state High Court?

She was also the first woman to be designated senior counsel by the Supreme Court of India. Justice Fathima M. Beevi was the first woman judge of the Supreme Court of India.

q_en: The most distinctive type of folk songs of Assam are ______.

q_en: Which article of the Indian constitution specifies equality before the law?

q_en: In which year was the Special Marriage Act passed in India?

The Special Marriage Act, 1954 replaced the old Act III, 1872.

q_en: The withdrawal of the monsoon begins in ______ states of India by early September.
e_en: The correct answer is north-western. Withdrawal of monsoon The withdrawal of the monsoon begins in the north-western states of India by early September. q_en: Which of the following Anglo - Maratha wars resulted in merging the Peshwas' territories with the Bombay Presidency?
e_en: The correct answer is Third. The Anglo-Maratha War that resulted in merging the Peshwas' territories with the Bombay Presidency was the Third Anglo-Maratha War. This war took place between 1817 and 1819 and was fought between the British East India Company and the Maratha Empire. The British won the war and as a result, the Peshwas' territories, which included Pune, were annexed by the British and merged with the Bombay Presidency.

q_en: Which of these is the correct reason for a good to be identified as a final good?
o_en: It is not processed by a consumer after purchase.
It cannot be recycled or re - used.
It is in the last stage of the product life cycle.
It is not processed further by a producer.
e_en: The correct answer is It is not processed further by a producer. A final good is a product that is purchased by the end-user for consumption, rather than for further processing or resale. The key term "final good" is used to distinguish between goods that are used by the end-user and goods that are used as inputs in the production of other goods.

q_en: The lofty gates erected in the courtyard of the temples in south India were called ______.
e_en: The correct answer is gopuram. Gopuram refers to the ornate and towering gateways that mark the entrance to the temple grounds in South India and Sri Lanka. Gopurams are typically made of stone and feature intricate carvings and sculptures of gods, goddesses, and other mythological figures. The gopuram's roots are in the early Pallava kings' constructions, which are related to North India's central shikhara towers.

q_en: Which of the following crops is the only genetically modified (GM) crop approved for commercial cultivation in India?
e_en: The correct answer is Bt Cotton. Bt Cotton is the only GM crop approved for commercial cultivation in India. It was first approved in 2002 for cultivation in six Indian states. Bt Cotton has been genetically modified to produce a toxin that kills bollworm, a major pest that affects cotton crops. The adoption of Bt Cotton in India has been controversial, with some arguing that it has led to increased farmer debt and decreased yields.

q_en: When the general interest rate reaches a very low level, which of the following statements will be correct?
o_en: Most people will expect the interest rate to rise in the future.
Most people will prefer to hold bonds.
Most people will speculate a further decline in the rate of interest.
Any increase in the money supply will cause the interest rate to fall further.
e_en: The correct answer is Most people will expect the interest rate to rise in the future. When the general interest rate reaches a very low level, most people will expect the interest rate to rise in the future because they anticipate that the central bank will try to stimulate the economy by increasing interest rates.

q_en: Who is known as the founder of Widow Remarriage Association (1861)?
e_en: The correct answer is Mahadev Govind Ranade. Widow Remarriage Association was founded in 1861 in Bombay (now Mumbai), India. The Association was established to promote the remarriage of widows, which was considered taboo in Indian society at that time. The founder of the Association, Mahadev Govind Ranade, was a prominent social reformer and a member of the Bombay Presidency Association, which was formed in 1885 to work for social and political reforms in India.

q_en: Which state in India has the highest number of aluminium smelting plants?
e_en: The correct answer is Odisha. Odissa has the highest number of aluminium smelting plants in India. q_en: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution prohibits forced labour and prevents exploitation?
e_en: The correct answer is Article 23. Article 23 of the Indian Constitution prohibits forced labour and any form of human trafficking. This includes trafficking of children and women for forced labour, prostitution, or any other form of exploitation. The article also prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 in any hazardous occupation or process. Any contravention of this article is a punishable offence under the law.

q_en: In 1956, which of the following awards did Rukmini Devi Arundale, an eminent Bharatanatyam dancer, receive?
e_en: The correct answer is Padma Bhushan. Rukmini Devi Arundale received the Padma Bhushan award in 1956 for her contribution to the field of Bharatanatyam dance. She was a pioneer in the revival and popularization of Bharatanatyam, which had been looked down upon as a low-class art form. Rukmini Devi Arundale was also a social activist and worked towards the betterment of women's rights and animal welfare.

q_en: Which river basin originates from the Western Ghats range of Karnataka state and has many tributaries such as the Noyyal, Kabini, Arkavathi and Amaravati?
e_en: The correct answer is Kaveri. The river basin that originates from the Western Ghats range of Karnataka state is the Kaveri River Basin. q_en: Who among the following personalities was appointed as the legal advisor of the Constituent Assembly that drafted the document of the Constitution?
e_en: The correct answer is BN Rau. BN Rau was appointed as the legal advisor of the Constituent Assembly that drafted the document of the Constitution. q_en: Mohiniyattam is a dance form of which state?
e_en: The correct answer is Kerala. Mohiniyattam is a classical dance form of Kerala, India. Mohiniyattam is primarily a solo dance performed by women and is known for its graceful movements and expressions. The dance form originated in the temples of Kerala and was performed by devadasis (temple dancers) to entertain the deities. The word Mohiniyattam is derived from two words, "Mohini" (meaning enchantress) and "attam" (meaning dance).

q_en: Which music director is popularly known as 'Pancham'?
e_en: The correct answer is RD Burman. RD Burman is popularly known as "Pancham" in the Indian music industry. He was the son of famous music director SD Burman. RD Burman was known for his innovative music compositions and experimentation with different genres of music. He composed music for over 300 films in his career and won several awards for his work.

q_en: Based on the recommendations of which Committee was the creation of a separate category for NBFCS operating in the microfinance sector (NBFC-MFI) done?
e_en: The correct answer is Malegam Committee. The creation of a separate category for NBFCs operating in the microfinance sector (NBFC-MFI) was done based on the recommendations of the Malegam Committee. The Malegam Committee was appointed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in 2010 to review the microfinance sector in India and provide recommendations for its growth and development.

q_en: Which of these is NOT a characteristic of a free-enterprise economy?
o_en: Decisions are based on the forces of demand and supply.
Factor rewards are based on the productivity of factors of production.
All economic decisions are taken by the economic planners.
Economic decisions are regulated by the market.
e_en: The correct answer is "All economic decisions are taken by the economic planners". A free-enterprise economy is also known as a capitalist economy, where the means of production are privately owned, and economic decisions are based on the forces of demand and supply. The government does not interfere in the market unless it is necessary to ensure fair competition or protect consumers. Economic decisions are regulated by the market in a free-enterprise economy.

q_en: Which regulatory body oversees microfinance institutions in India?

q_en: In which State of India is Sher Shah's Tomb located?
e_en: The correct answer is Bihar. Sher Shah's Tomb is located in the state of Bihar in India. Sher Shah was a prominent ruler of medieval India who ruled over the region from 1540 to 1545. He is known for his administrative and military reforms, which laid the foundation for the Mughal Empire. Sher Shah's Tomb is located in the town of Sasaram in Bihar.

q_en: Which of the following associations was formed in Maharashtra to get social justice for the weaker sections of society?

q_en: Which of the following article says that 'It shall be the duty of every citizen of India who is a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of six and fourteen years'?
e_en: The correct answer is Article 51A(k). This article specifically addresses the duty of parents and guardians to provide education to their children.

q_en: Who gave the concept of 'money illusion' for the first time?

q_en: Which of the following cities was built by Humayun at Delhi?

q_en: According to Census of India 2011, which state in India has the highest female literacy rate?

q_en: 2ⁿd October is observed as _____________ .

q_en: The political Part of the Indian Constitution has been largely drawn from which Constitution?

q_en: Which are the four quantum numbers for an electron present in 4f orbital?
e_en: The correct answer is n = 4, I = 3, m = +1, s = +1/2. The four quantum numbers for an electron present in 4f orbital are n = 4, l = 3, m = +1, and s = +1/2. The azimuthal quantum number (l) determines the shape of the orbital, and for f orbital, it can have values from 0 to n-1, which gives l = 3.

q_en: In the middle of which century did the Arab traveler Sulaiman visit India?

q_en: Ramnad V Raghavan is associated with which of the following musical instruments?

q_en: The government is bound to ensure observance of social welfare and labour laws enacted to secure for workmen a life compatible with human dignity, under ________ of the Indian Constitution.

q_en: Which great leader died due to his injuries in the Anti-Simon Commission Protest of 1928?

q_en: Which district of Madhya Pradesh is a leading producer of copper?

q_en: In which of the following years did the East India Company abolish the diarchy system of Bengal?

q_en: Bastar Dussehra is celebrated in which of the following states?

q_en: In India, which Ministry issues the coins of all denominations?

q_en: In the MPL 59th Senior National Chess Championship held in Delhi, Who became India's 78th Grandmaster ?

q_en: Which of the following Articles says that double jeopardy which says that "no person shall be prosecuted or punished for the same offence more than once." ?

q_en: Which institution had launched the project E-Shakti for the digitization of all members of self-help groups in India?

q_en: The Western Ghats and the Eastern Ghats meet at which of the following places in southern India?

q_en: Which of these is related to public goods?

q_en: Which of the following is the correct sequence of national income from broader to narrower concepts?

q_en: The measures of money supply, namely, M1, M2, M3 and M4, in this order, indicate:

e_en: The correct answer is decreasing the order of liquidity. The money supply measures are used by central banks to monitor and control the amount of money in circulation in the economy. M1 includes the most liquid forms of money such as cash, demand deposits, and traveler's checks. It is considered a narrow measure of money supply. M2 includes M1 plus less liquid forms of money such as savings deposits, time deposits, and money market funds.

q_en: Which of the following is a feature of the Directive Principles of State Policy of the Indian Constitution?
e_en: The correct answer is non-justiciable. The directive principles of State policy ( aka DPSP ) were borrowed from Ireland in 1937. However, the idea of DPSP originated in Spain. q_en: From which five-year plan onwards in India, were fiscal and economic reforms including liberalization adopted?

It was the beginning of liberalization, privatization, and globalization (LPG) in India.

q_en: Usually, the reduction in taxes will have a ______ multiplier effect compared to an increase in government spending on aggregate demand.
e_en: The correct answer is smaller. Smaller - When taxes are reduced, people have more disposable income to spend which leads to an increase in consumption and hence, an increase in aggregate demand. However, the multiplier effect of this increase in demand is smaller than the multiplier effect of an increase in government spending because some of the tax savings may be saved or used to pay off debt rather than spent immediately.

q_en: The target for the first commitment period of the Kyoto Protocol is to reduce emissions of how many greenhouse gases by 5.2% from 1990 levels?

q_en: Revenue expenditure minus revenue receipts is ______.
e_en: The correct answer is revenue deficit. Revenue deficit arises when a government's revenue expenditure surpasses its revenue receipts. Revenue expenditure encompasses spending on items like salaries, pensions, and interest payments, while revenue receipts comprise income from taxes and fees. This deficit serves as a crucial gauge of the government's fiscal condition, with elevated deficits potentially triggering issues like inflation and economic instability.

e_en: The correct answer is Doubling of farmers’ income. "Doubling of farmers' income," is not directly related to the industrial sector. Increasing farmers' income typically involves agricultural policies, improvements in farming techniques, infrastructure development in rural areas, and market reforms to ensure fair prices for agricultural products.

q_en: Rast-Goftar, a newspaper, propagated the messages of socio-religious reforms for which of the following societies?
e_en: The correct answer is Parsi. The newspaper Rast Goftar, also known as Truthteller, advocated for social and religious reforms within the Parsi community. q_en: Which of the following is the most widespread forest type in India?
e_en: The correct answer is Tropical Deciduous Forests. Tropical deciduous forests, also referred to as monsoon forests, thrive in regions receiving an annual rainfall ranging from 70 to 200 cm. These forests exhibit lush greenery and dense vegetation during the wet summer months but transform during the dry winters, characterized by leaf shedding and a drier landscape.

q_en: What is the number of players in a Kho Kho team?
e_en: The correct answer is 12. A Kho Kho team comprises 12 players, with nine players participating in a game while the remaining three serve as substitutes. During a game, the chasing team sends nine players onto the field who assume a kneeling position. Meanwhile, the defending team, comprised of the remaining three players, aims to evade being touched by members of the opposing team.

q_en: Which of the following is a plantation crop found abundantly in Assam?
e_en: The correct answer is Tea. Tea is a plantation crop found abundantly in Assam. Tea cultivation is a prominent industry in Assam, one of India's northeastern states. The region's favourable climate, with abundant rainfall and rich, loamy soil, provides optimal conditions for tea cultivation. Additionally, the low elevation and high humidity levels further contribute to the ideal environment for tea plantations.

q_en:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are FALSE?
A) The impact of externality is always positive.
B) Real national income means national income at constant prices
e_en: The correct answer is Only A. An externality refers to the occurrence of a cost or benefit resulting from the actions of one party, yet borne or enjoyed financially by another. These effects may impact individuals or entire organizations and can be classified as either private or societal. Positive externalities arise when they provide a benefit to a third party.

q_en: Which of the following grains contain oryzenin?
e_en: The correct answer is Rice. Oryzenin, a storage protein present in rice grains, constitutes the primary glutelin found in rice, comprising approximately 75–90% of the total protein content in rice grains. Extracting oryzenin from rice grains and rice flour involves the process of sonification. Renowned for its high quality, oryzenin boasts a complete amino acid profile.

q_en:
With reference to Sonepur Cattle Fair, consider the following statements and select the correct option.
a) It is associated with the Hariharanatha temple.
b) It begins on Purnima (full moon night) and Kartik month.
c) It is celebrated in the Madhya Pradesh state.
e_en: The correct answer is Both a and b. The Sonepur Cattle Fair, also known as Harihar Kshetra Mela, takes place on Kartik Poornima (the full moon day) spanning the months of November and December in Sonepur, Bihar, situated at the confluence of the Ganges and Gandak rivers. Originally, the fair was held in Hajipur, with only the puja performed at the Harihar Nath temple in Sonpur. However, during the reign of Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb, the fair's location shifted to Sonpur.

e_en: The correct answer is To organise village panchayat. The Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles of State Policy, and Fundamental Duties are integral sections of the Constitution of India, delineating the essential obligations of the state towards its citizens, as well as the rights and duties of citizens towards the State. These sections are regarded as fundamental components of the constitution, which was crafted by the Constituent Assembly of India between 1947 and 1949.

q_en: Which of these is NOT one of the rationales behind microfinance?

More than access to credit poor need subsidies
The absence of formal employment makes the poor non 'bankable'.

q_en: In 2006, Ileana Citaristi, an Italian Odissi dancer, was awarded with the ______.

e_en: The correct answer is Nehruvian. Nehruvian is NOT included in the category of Directive Principles of State Policy of the Indian Constitution. The Directive Principles of State Policy in India are categorized into several groups: Economic and Socialistic, Political and Administrative, Justice and Legal, Environmental, Protection of Monuments, Peace and Security. These principles serve as guidelines for the governance of the country by the government of India.

q_en: The music legend Jagjit Singh is associated with:
e_en: The correct answer is Ghazal. Jagjit Singh was a renowned Indian composer, singer, and musician recognized for his contributions across multiple languages. He is widely credited with revitalizing and popularizing ghazal, a traditional Indian art form, by selecting poetry that resonated with the masses and composing it in a manner that emphasized the significance of words and the melodies they invoked.

q_en: What is the classical dance of Assam?
e_en: The correct answer is Sattriya Nritya. Sattriya Nritya is the classical dance of Assam. Sattriya Nritya holds a significant position among Indian classical dances. Initially conceived as part of Bhaona, performances of Ankiya Nat, one-act plays, the art form was pioneered by Sankardev, a polymath from Assam during the 15th-16th century.

q_en: The Pala Dynasty rulers were primarily patrons of which religion?
e_en: The correct answer is Buddhist. The Pala Dynasty rulers were primarily patrons Buddhist. The Pāla Empire emerged as a dominant force in the Indian subcontinent during the post-classical period, with its roots in the Bengal region.

q_en: Those engaged in agriculture in India suffer from which of these unemployment types?
e_en: The correct answer is Disguised Unemployment. Disguised unemployment refers to a situation where a portion of the labour force either remains jobless or is employed in a manner that contributes negligibly to productivity. Despite being technically unemployed, these workers do not impact the overall output of the economy. This phenomenon arises when productivity levels are low, and an excessive number of workers are engaged in jobs that do not require their full capacity.

q_en: Which Indian state was the first to make it mandatory for all homes to have rooftop rainwater harvesting structures?
e_en: The correct answer is Tamil Nadu. Tamil Nadu set a pioneering precedent in India by instituting mandatory rooftop rainwater harvesting in 2001, a policy that remains unique to the state. Amendments were introduced to the Tamil Nadu District Municipalities Act of 1920 and the Building Rules of 1973, mandating the incorporation of rainwater harvesting structures in all new constructions.

q_en: Which of the following sentences is INCORRECT with regard to government budget?
o_en: Government budget is a constitutional requirement in India.
It is a statement of estimated receipts and expenditures of the government for the financial year.
It is a statement of receipts and expenditures incurred by the government.
e_en: The correct answer is It is a statement of receipts and expenditures incurred by the government. Government budget is a constitutional requirement in India : Article 112 of the Indian Constitution mandates the government to present an annual budget to the Parliament.

q_en: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution enshrines that if we are observing any religious procession, then we need to remember communal harmony?
e_en: The correct answer is Article 51A (e). Article 51A(e) of Indian Constitution: To promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic, and regional or sectional diversities; to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women. q_en: Which state in India has the highest literacy rate as per Census of 2011?

q_en: Bokajan is a cement plant located in which of the following states?

Annually, the plant produces around 198,000 MT by using the dry process.

q_en: Which of the following aggregates best describes the National Income?
e_en: The correct answer is NNP at FC. NNP at FC (Net National Product at factor cost) best describes the National Income. q_en: Subha Mudgal is famous for which of the following music forms?

Hindustani classical music: The classical music of the northern parts of the Indian subcontinent is known as Hindustani classical music.

q_en: What is the name of a type of waterfall with an enormous volume of water?
e_en: The correct answer is Cataract. Cataract: This term specifically refers to a large, powerful waterfall with an enormous volume of water flowing over a steep drop. e_en: The correct answer is 1909. Indian Councils Act of 1909 also called Morley-Minto Reforms. q_en: Hornbill festival is celebrated in which of the following states?

q_en: Which country came out with the first 'official' compilation of volleyball rules and was published by the YMCA?

q_en: Velocity of circulation of money is ______
o_en: k times the value of transactions
the number of times a unit of money changes hands during the unit period
the number of times the same transactions can be repeated by a given volume of money supply
the ratio of money balance to the value of transactions
e_en: The correct answer is the number of times a unit of money changes hands during the unit period. It is the frequency with which the total money supply in the economy turns over in a given period of time. It is measured by dividing GDP by the country's total money supply. A high velocity of circulation in a country indicates a high degree of inflation.

q_en: Which of these is NOT true about green revolution?
o_en: It was funded by international agencies.
It was a private-sector programme for agricultural modernization.
It was targeted mainly in the wheat and rice-growing areas.
It was introduced only in areas that had assured irrigation.

The Green Revolution in India: The Green Revolution, which refers to the large-scale introduction of high-yielding varieties of seeds, fertilizers, and pesticides in agriculture, has been criticized for its negative impact on small farmers. The Government of India launched the Green Revolution in 1965 under the Third Five-Year Plan(1961-66).

q_en: The traditional 'Cheraw' dance, in which bamboo is used, is famous in _______.
e_en: The correct answer is Mizoram. The "Cheraw" dance, also known as the "Bamboo dance," is a captivating performance showcasing the cultural heritage of the Mizo people of Mizoram. q_en: Which of the following posts of Defence Research Development Organisation (DRDO) is in the Level I (top level) of its organisational chart?

q_en: Bailadila range of hills are famous for which of the following minerals?

q_en: The Battle of Karnal is known for the invasion of which of the following aggressors against India?
e_en: The correct answer is Nadir Shah. The Battle of Karnal occurred in 1739, when Nadir Shah, the ruler of the Afsharid dynasty of Persia, invaded India. q_en: Which of the following is NOT an approach for measuring unemployment in India?

e_en: The correct answer is Tuluva. Krishnadeva Raya (1471 - 1529) belonged to the Tuluva dynasty and served as its third ruler, reigning from 1509 to 1529. q_en: Who among the following devoted his life to the upliftment of widows and established the Widow Remarriage Association in 1893?

(a) Habeas corpus - (iii) To have a body of Habeas corpus is a legal action that requires a person under arrest to be brought before a judge or into court, especially to secure the person's release unless lawful grounds are shown for their detention. In essence, it protects individuals from being unlawfully detained.

q_en: Lotia is a regional music form of which state?
e_en: The correct answer is Rajasthan. Lotia is a traditional folk music genre originating from Rajasthan, India. It finds its cultural expression through the voices of peasants as they toil in the fields, particularly during the Lotia festival, which typically occurs in the Chaitra month of the Hindi calendar. Thematically, Lotia revolves around the significance of water.

q_en:
Which of the following statements is/are FALSE with respect to simple model of the circular flow of economy?
i. The aggregate consumption is more than the aggregate expenditure.
ii. There is government intervention.
iii. There are no trade activities with the rest of the world.
e_en: The correct answer is Only i. The basic circular flow model of the economy operates without government intervention. This model illustrates the interconnected flow of money, goods, and services among economic participants. It serves as the foundation for national accounting and macroeconomics.

q_en: Which of the following Indian classical dancers was the recipient of the Padma Vibhushan award of 2003?
e_en: The correct answer is Sonal Mansingh. Sonal Mansingh is a prominent figure in Indian classical dance, specializing in Bharatanatyam and Odissi styles. Not only is she a highly respected dancer and Guru, but she has also been nominated by the President of India to serve as a Member of Parliament in the Rajya Sabha. Mansingh's contributions to the field have been recognized with prestigious awards, including the Padma Bhushan in 1992 and the Padma Vibhushan in 2003.

q_en: The Physical Quality of Life Index does NOT include which of the following indicators?
e_en: The correct answer is Gender development index. The Physical Quality of Life Index does NOT include Gender development index. The Gender Development Index (GDI) is a metric crafted to assess gender equality. It, along with the Gender Empowerment Measure (GEM), was introduced in the 1995 Human Development Report by the United Nations Development Program. These measures were devised to imbue the Human Development Index (HDI) with a gender-sensitive perspective.

q_en: Rajini Gabra and Harni Gabra is the cultural festival of which of the following Indian states?
e_en: The correct answer is Assam. Rajini Gabra and Harni Gabra are annual festivals observed by the Dimasa tribe. These socio-religious events are held before the commencement of new agricultural activities. The Rabha tribe celebrates the Baikho festival during the spring season to honor and seek blessings from the goddess of wealth, 'Baikho'.

q_en: Who was appointed as the first woman Vice-Chancellor of Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU), New Delhi?
e_en: The correct answer is Santishree Pandit. In February 2022, Santishree Dhulipudi Pandit made history as the first woman Vice-Chancellor of Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) in Delhi, appointed by the Ministry of Education. She is an alumna of JNU, holds an MPhil and PhD in International Relations from the university.

q_en: Which of these is NOT one of the impacts of the green revolution?
o_en: A loosening of traditional bonds or hereditary relationships between farmers or landowners and agricultural workers.
The rise of a class of 'free' wage labourers.
A shift from payment in cash to payment in kind (grain).
There was an increase in the use of agricultural labour as cultivation became more intensive.
e_en: The correct answer is A shift from payment in cash to payment in kind (grain). A shift from payment in cash to payment in kind (grain) is NOT one of the impacts of the green revolution. Payment-in-kind (PIK) involves utilizing a commodity or service as compensation rather than cash.

q_en: Which of the following steps is NOT involved in a Water Cycle?
e_en: The correct answer is Hydration. The hydration step is NOT involved in a Water Cycle. Hydration involves replenishing the body fluids that are lost through sweating, exhaling, and waste elimination. Typically, the body loses and requires to replacement of approximately 2-3 quarts of water each day. Fortunately, many of the foods we consume are predominantly made up of water. Examples of such foods include leafy greens, as well as most fruits and vegetables.

q_en: Which of the following is true about the Great Indian Desert?
o_en: Bounded to the west by the Aravali
Lies to the southeast of the Aravali
Lies to the northwest of the Aravali
Bounded to the south by the Aravali
e_en: The correct answer is Lies to the northwest of the Aravali. The Thar Desert, also referred to as the Great Indian Desert, lies to the northwest of the Aravalli Range, a mountain range extending from Delhi to Gujarat in northwest India. It comprises an undulating sandy plain adorned with sand dunes, serving as a natural demarcation between India and Pakistan.

q_en: According to the Census of India 2011, what is the literacy rate among the male population in India?
e_en: The correct answer is 82.14%. The literacy rate among the male population in India has shown a steady increase over the years. In 2001, it was 75.26%, and in 2011, it increased to 82.14%. &l

q_en: Which of the following Provisions of the Indian Constitution is taken from the US Constitution?
e_en: The correct answer is the Post of vice president. The provision of the post of vice president in the Indian Constitution is taken from the US Constitution. The vice president of India is the second-highest constitutional office in the country and is elected indirectly by an Electoral College consisting of members of both houses of Parliament.

q_en: What is the nominal GDP if the real GDP is 500 and the price index is 150?
e_en: The correct answer is 750. In this question, the real GDP is given as 500 and the price index is given as 150. To calculate the nominal GDP, we need to multiply the real GDP by the price index and divide by 100. Hence, the nominal GDP would be (500 x 150) / 100 = 750. Therefore, the correct answer is 750.

q_en: How many digits does the MMID code of any commercial bank have?
e_en: The correct answer is 7. The MMID code of any commercial bank has 7 digits. MMID stands for Mobile Money Identifier. It is a unique 7-digit code assigned by banks to their customers for mobile banking transactions.

q_en: What are the events in powerlifting?
o_en: Squats, bench press and dead lift
Squats, lat pull down and curl
Curls, over arm lift and dead lift
e_en: The correct answer is Squats, bench press and dead lift. Powerlifting is a strength sport that involves lifting as much weight as possible in three different exercises: squats, bench press, and deadlift. These exercises are collectively known as the "big three" in powerlifting. Squats involve lifting a barbell on your shoulders and lowering your body until your thighs are parallel to the ground. This exercise primarily targets your quadriceps, glutes, and hamstrings.

q_en:
Identify the correct match.
A) Pension to retired government employees - Revenue Receipt
B) Purchase of Machinery in Railways - Capital Expenditure
e_en: The correct answer is Only B. The purchase of machinery in Railways is a Capital Expenditure as it involves the acquisition of a fixed asset that will be used over a period of time to generate revenue for the Railways. Capital Expenditure refers to the expenditure incurred on acquiring or improving fixed assets such as land, buildings, machinery, etc.

q_en: By what name did Vinayak Savarkar form a secret organization of revolutionaries in the year 1904?
e_en: The correct answer is Abhinav Bharat. Vinayak Savarkar formed a secret organization of revolutionaries called Abhinav Bharat in the year 1904. First established as "Mitra Mela" in Nasik, it was Vinayak Savarkar's final year at Fergusson College in Pune. Following a few assassinations of British officials, the Savarkar brothers were found guilty and sentenced to prison. In 1952, the society was formally dissolved.

q_en: Which of the following has Kharif crops only?
e_en: The correct answer is Cotton and paddy. Kharif crops are those crops that are sown in the rainy season and harvested in the winter season. They require high rainfall and warm temperature for their growth. Cotton and paddy are two major Kharif crops that are widely grown in India.

q_en: Which of the following is an open-pit copper mine?
e_en: The correct answer is Malanjkhand. Malanjkhand is an open-pit copper mine located in the Balaghat district of Madhya Pradesh, India. It is the largest copper deposit in India and one of the largest in the world. The mine is owned by Hindustan Copper Limited, a public sector undertaking under the Ministry of Mines, Government of India.

q_en: Mopin is an agricultural festival celebrated in the state of ______.
e_en: The correct answer is Arunachal Pradesh. Mopin is a festival celebrated by the Galo tribe of Arunachal Pradesh, India. This festival is usually celebrated in the month of April. Mopin is celebrated to thank the gods for a good harvest and to pray for the well-being of the community. During this festival, people wear traditional attire, perform traditional dances, and offer prayers and sacrifices to the gods.

q_en: Nati is the folk dance of which of the following Indian states?
e_en: The correct answer is Himachal Pradesh. Nati is a popular folk dance of Himachal Pradesh, performed during various occasions such as weddings, festivals, and other celebrations. The dance involves a group of men and women dancing in a circle, with the participants holding hands and moving in a rhythmic pattern. The music for Nati is usually provided by traditional instruments such as dhol, nagara, shehnai, and flute, among others.

q_en: Which of the following classification bases of industry applies to the products - cotton, jute, wool, silk textile, rubber, tea, sugar, coffee, and edible oil?
e_en: The correct answer is Agro-based industries. Agro-based industries are the correct answer as all the products listed are derived from agricultural sources. Agro-based industries refer to those industries that rely heavily on agricultural products as their raw materials. Key industries are those industries that are considered crucial for the growth and development of an economy, such as steel, petroleum, and automobile industries.

q_en: Who composed 'Shahnama'?
e_en: The correct answer is Ferdowsi. 'Shahnama', also known as 'Book of Kings', is a long epic poem written by Ferdowsi in the Persian language. The poem narrates the history of Persia and its kings from the creation of the world up until the Islamic conquest of Persia in the 7th century.

q_en:
X has been exercising his freedom of trade in Chennai to earn his livelihood.
Such kind of freedom is provided in which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution?
e_en: The correct answer is Article 19. Article 19 of the Indian Constitution provides the freedom to practice any profession, occupation, trade, or business. Article 18 deals with the abolition of titles, whereas Article 17 abolishes untouchability. Article 16 talks about equality of opportunity in matters of public employment.

q_en: Rabindra Sangeet is associated with:
e_en: The correct answer is Rabindranath Tagore. Rabindra Sangeet is a genre of music that originated in Bengal and is primarily associated with the works of Rabindranath Tagore. The music of Rabindra Sangeet is characterized by its poetic lyrics, melodic tunes,</strong&

q_en: Which of these MFIs are NOT regulated by the RBI?
e_en: The correct answer is Non-profit MFIs. Non-profit MFIs are not regulated by the RBI. Small Finance Bank-led MFIs are regulated by the RBI as they are categorized as banks. Bank-led MFIs are also regulated by the RBI as they are subsidiaries of banks. NBFC MFIs are regulated by the RBI as they are categorized as Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs). Non-profit MFIs are typically registered as societies or trusts and operate on a not-for-profit basis.

q_en: Pandit Birju Maharaj is associated with which form of dance?
e_en: The correct answer is Kathak. Pandit Birju Maharaj is associated with the classical Indian dance form of Kathak. He is a renowned Kathak dancer, choreographer, and instructor from India. Kathak is a North Indian classical dance form that involves intricate footwork, pirouettes, and facial expressions to depict various emotions and stories.

q_en: 54.69% of the total workforce is engaged in _______ and allied sector activities (Census of India 2011).
e_en: The correct answer is Agriculture. According to the Census of India 2011, 54.69% of the total workforce is engaged in agriculture and allied sector activities. Agriculture is the primary occupation for a majority of the rural population in India and contributes significantly to the country's economy.

q_en: Structural composition of the economy refers to:
o_en: contribution of various sectors to the GDP
rural and urban distribution of the population
e_en: The correct answer is the contribution of various sectors to the GDP. Structural composition of the economy refers to the contribution of various sectors to the GDP. It is a measure of the percentage of economic activity that each sector contributes to the overall GDP of a country. The sectors typically include agriculture, manufacturing, services, and others.

q_en: The rulers of which of the following Rajput dynasties patronised Jainism and one of them is reported to have accepted Jainism under the influence of a Jain scholar Hemachandra?
e_en: The correct answer is Chalukya. Chalukya dynasty ruled over parts of present-day Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh from the 6th to the 12th century CE. The Chalukya rulers were known for their patronage of Jainism, as well as Hinduism and Buddhism. Some of the notable Jain scholars who flourished under their patronage were Akalanka, Siddharshi, and Hemachandra. Hemachandra was a renowned Jain monk, poet, and scholar who lived during the 12th century CE.

q_en: Since 2004, which of the following states in India is the permanent venue of the International Film Festival of India?
e_en: The correct answer is Goa. Goa has been the permanent venue for IFFI since 2004. International Film Festival of India (IFFI) is an annual film festival organized by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Government of India. The festival was started in 1952 and has been held in different cities across India. The festival showcases a wide range of films from across the world, including feature films, documentaries, and short films.

q_en: Who was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for founding the Grameen Bank and pioneering the concepts of microcredit and microfinance?
e_en: The correct answer is Muhammad Yunus. Muhammad Yunus is a prominent member of civil society, banker, economist, and social entrepreneur from Bangladesh. In recognition of his creating the Grameen Bank and developing the ideas of microcredit and microfinance, he was granted the Nobel Peace Prize in 2006. Entrepreneurs who are too impoverished to be eligible for conventional bank loans are granted these loans.

q_en: Exports of mangoes by India are a part of _______ method of measurement of its national income.
e_en: The correct answer is expenditure. Exports of mangoes by India contribute to the expenditure method of measuring its national income because it represents a portion of the country's total exports, which is a component of its overall expenditure. The expenditure method of measuring national income is one of three primary methods used, along with the income method and the value-added method.

q_en: According to the Census of India 2011, which state in India has the highest proportion of its population living in the urban areas?
e_en: The correct answer is Goa. According to the Census of India 2011, Goa has the highest proportion of its population living in urban areas. The urban population of Goa is 62.17% of the total population. Goa is followed by Tamil Nadu with an urban population of 48.45%. Kerala has an urban population of 47.72% and Haryana has an urban population of 34.91%.

q_en: Which is the biggest tributary of the upper Brahmaputra that originates in the Tibetan Himalayas and winds its way into India through Arunachal Pradesh?
e_en: The correct answer is Subansiri. Subansiri is the biggest tributary of the upper Brahmaputra. It originates in the Tibetan Himalayas and flows through Arunachal Pradesh before joining the Brahmaputra in Assam. The Brahmaputra River is one of the major rivers in Asia, flowing through China, India, and Bangladesh. It is also known as the Tsangpo-Brahmaputra River system. Some of the other tributaries of the Brahmaputra include the Lohit, Dibang, and Kameng rivers.

q_en: Tulip Festival is famous in which city?
e_en: The correct answer is Srinagar. The Tulip Festival is an annual event organized in Srinagar, the capital city of Jammu and Kashmir state in India. The festival is held during the spring season, usually in the months of March and April, when the tulip gardens in Srinagar are in full bloom. The festival attracts a large number of tourists from all over the world who come to witness the colorful display of tulips in the gardens of Srinagar.

q_en: In which of the following economic accounts are transfer payments included?
e_en: The correct answer is Government account. Transfer payments are included in the government account of economic accounts. Transfer payments are payments made by the government to individuals or businesses without any expectation of goods or services in return. Examples of transfer payments include social security, welfare, and unemployment benefits.

q_en: The celebration of Christmas, Eid, and Holi in school is an example of making children learn fundamental duties as well. Which of the following fundamental duties advocates about this type of ideals?
o_en: To defend the country and render national service
To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
To promote harmony and spirit of common brotherhood
e_en: The correct answer is To promote harmony and spirit of common brotherhood. Celebrating festivals of different religions in school promotes the idea of unity in diversity, which is the essence of promoting harmony and common brotherhood. By participating in these celebrations, children learn to respect and appreciate different cultures and religions, which is important for building a cohesive society.

q_en: Which of the following states is NOT a part of the Peninsular Plateau in India?
e_en: The correct answer is Punjab. The Peninsular Plateau in India is a large region of elevated land that lies to the south of the Indo-Gangetic Plain. It is mainly composed of Precambrian rocks that are millions of years old. The plateau covers parts of several Indian states, including Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Kerala. However, Punjab is not a part of the Peninsular Plateau.

q_en:
Poshan Abhiyaan is a program to achieve nutritional status of children from 0 to 6 years.
Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution provides for raising the nutrition level?
e_en: The correct answer is Article 47. Article 47 states that "the State shall regard the raising of the level of nutrition and the standard of living of its people and the improvement of public health as among its primary duties". This article emphasizes the importance of improving the overall health and well-being of the citizens of India, including their nutritional status.

q_en: Who among the following is the first Indian female football player to play in the Union of European Football Association (UEFA) Women's Champions League?
e_en: The correct answer is Manisha Kalyan. Manisha Kalyan is the first Indian female football player to play in the Union of European Football Association (UEFA) women's Champions League. She played for Gokulam Kerala FC in the 2018-19 season. Manisha Kalyan is a forward player and has represented India in various international tournaments. She has also played for the Indian Women's League teams like Rising Student Club and Sethu FC.

q_en: Ustad Asad Ali Khan played which of the following instruments?
e_en: The correct answer is Rudra Veena. Ustad Asad Ali Khan played the Rudra Veena, which is a stringed instrument used in Indian classical music. The Rudra Veena is known for its deep, resonant sound and is considered one of the oldest instruments in India. The Hindu referred to Khan, who played in the dhrupad style, as the greatest rudra veena player alive in India. In 2008, he received the Indian civilian distinction of Padma Bhushan.

q_en: Which of the following classical dance forms is associated with Hindustani Classical Music?
e_en: The correct answer is Kathak. Kathak is one of the eight major classical dance forms of India and originated in North India. The dance form has its roots in the Mughal era and is characterized by intricate footwork, graceful hand movements, and storytelling through facial expressions. Kathak is closely associated with Hindustani classical music and is often performed to the accompaniment of tabla, sarangi, and sitar.

q_en: Which of these is NOT an NGO involved in microfinance-related activities?
e_en: The correct answer is NABARD in Mumbai. NGO stands for Non-Governmental Organization, which is a non-profit organization that operates independently of any government. NGOs are usually involved in social, cultural, and environmental activities to promote social welfare. Microfinance is a financial service provided to low-income individuals or groups who do not have access to traditional banking services.

q_en: Which of the following committees had recommended to incorporate the Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution?
e_en: The correct answer is the Swaran Singh Committee. The Fundamental Duties were incorporated in Part IV-A of the Indian Constitution through the 42ⁿd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976. At present, there are eleven fundamental duties under Article 51 A of the Constitution. The idea of Fundamental Duties has been borrowed from the erstwhile USSR. Originally the duties were ten in number, later on through the 86th Amendment Act, of 2002, the eleventh Fundamental duty was added.

q_en: Pratham Bank, the first Regional Rural Bank of India, had its Head Office in which state?
e_en: The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh. Pratham Bank was established in 1975 as the first Regional Rural Bank of India. Its Head Office was located in Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh. The bank was sponsored by Syndicate Bank and had its operations in 8 districts of Uttar Pradesh. The first Regional Rural Bank “Prathama Grameen Bank” was set up on October 2, 1975. At present, there are 82 RRBs in India.

q_en: 'Uttar Ramcharita' was the composition of which of the following poets?
e_en: The correct answer is Bhavabhuti. Bhavabhuti was a renowned Sanskrit poet and playwright who lived during the 8th century CE in India. Bhavabhuti (original name: Srikanth) was the court poet of King Yashovarman of Kannauj. He was the most illustrious dramatist and poet of the 8th century.​ Bhavabhuti wrote Malatimadhava, Mahaviracharita and Uttaramacharita.

The 9.02 Kilometre Long Tunnel has been constructed by the Border Roads Organisation (BRO) at a cost of INR 3, 300 crores.

q_en: Which of the following states has the honor of being India's first carbon-free state?
e_en: The correct one is Himachal Pradesh. Himachal Pradesh was declared as India's first carbon-neutral state in 2010. q_en: Cultivating large farms with moderately low inputs of labor and capital is referred to as ________.
e_en: The correct answer is extensive cultivation. Extensive cultivation refers to the practice of cultivating large farms with moderately low inputs of labor and capital. It is also known as extensive subsistence agriculture. This type of cultivation is usually practiced in areas with low population density and abundant land resources.

q_en: What was the percentage of women working in the primary sector of India as of 2011-2012?
e_en: The correct answer is 62.8%. The primary sector includes agriculture, forestry, fishing, and mining. As of 2011-2012, the percentage of women working in the primary sector in India was 62.8 percent. Women's participation in the workforce has been increasing in recent years, but there is still a significant gender gap. According to the World Bank, in 2019, the labor force participation rate for women in India was 22.3%, compared to 76.5% for men.

q_en: Which of the following is NOT a common product offered by microfinance institutions in India?
e_en: The correct answer is Credit cards. Microfinance institutions in India primarily focus on providing financial services to the economically weaker sections of society who do not have access to formal banking services. The most common products offered by microfinance institutions in India are personal loans, insurance products, and savings accounts.

q_en: What is the minimum lane width in Swimming in meters?
e_en: The correct answer is 2.13. The minimum lane width is prescribed by the International Swimming Federation (FINA), which is the governing body for Swimming. The minimum lane width is important to ensure that swimmers have enough space to swim comfortably and safely without colliding with each other. FINA has prescribed different minimum lane widths for different types of competitions.

q_en: The Vernacular Press Act was enacted during the regime of which viceroy of India?
e_en: The correct answer is Lord Lytton. Vernacular Press Act 1878: ​British India passed the Vernacular Press Act (1878) to restrict press freedom and discourage criticism of British policy, notably the opposition that had risen since the commencement of the Second Anglo-Afghan War (1878–80). The Act was submitted by Lytton, the Viceroy of India at the time, and on March 14, 1878, the Viceroy's Council unanimously approved it.

q_en: Tusu Parab is the harvest festival of which of the following Indian states?
e_en: The correct answer is Jharkhand. The Tusu festival is primarily observed in Assam, the Tea-producing State, Northeastern Odisha, Southwest West Bengal, and Southeast Jharkhand. During this occasion, the goddess Tusu is worshipped. The focus is primarily on rivers. It is a unified expression of the agrarian society's shared trust and belief in the pleasure of crop gathering. It is thought that the term "Tusu" derives from the word "tush" for rice bran.

q_en: From which place did the Revolt of 1857 start?
e_en: The correct answer is Meerut. The Revolt of 1857 was the first rebellion against the British East India Company. The first war of Indian Independence started on 10th May 1857. The revolt was started at Meerut. It began as a revolt of the sepoys of the British East India Company’s army but eventually secured the participation of the masses. The issue of greased cartridges and military grievances has been over-emphasized as the factor for the Revolt of 1857.

q_en: Who among the following personalities is associated with the musical instrument Flute?
e_en: The correct answer is Pandit Hari Prasad Chaurasia. He was born in Prayagraj. Famous classical flutist of the Hindustani classical tradition. Chaurasia belonged to the Maihar Senia Gharana (a community of performers who share a distinctive musical style), and he developed a rich personal style after years of experimentation and dedicated practice. Learned under the tutelage of famous flute player Bholanath Prasanna.

q_en: Which is the most powerful river in the world in terms of its volume and extensive drainage into the Atlantic Ocean?
e_en: The correct answer is Amazon. The Amazon River holds the distinction of being the world's largest river in terms of both discharge volume and drainage basin area, surpassing even the combined flow and basin areas of the Nile, Yangtze, and Mississippi Rivers. Additionally, it stands as the planet's largest drainage system by volume of flow and basin area.

q_en: Which of the following regions in India is nicknamed as the storehouse of minerals?
e_en: The correct answer is Chota Nagpur. The Chota Nagpur Plateau in India has earned the moniker "storehouse of minerals" due to its abundant mineral wealth. Comprised primarily of igneous rocks dating back to the Pre-Cambrian era, this plateau boasts a rich array of resources including mica, bauxite, copper, limestone, iron ore, and coal.

q_en:
Which of the following will be considered normal residents of India?
A) Indians working in foreign embassies in India.
B) Ambassador for India in the rest of the world.
e_en: The correct answer is Both A and B. Both Indian citizens working in foreign embassies within India and the Ambassador representing India abroad are classified as normal residents of India. A normal resident in the context of India is defined as an individual who resides or is situated within the country and engages in fundamental economic activities, including earning, spending, and accruing wealth from that location.

q_en: Which of the following is the most problematic and primary difficulty of barter exchanges as against money - based exchanges?
o_en: Bartered exchanges involve difficulty in preserving value.
Barter exchanges may result in an incorrect valuation of the goods transacted.
Barter exchanges may be imperfectly divisible.
Barter exchanges require a double coincidence of wants.

Barter exchanges require a double coincidence of wants is the most problematic and primary difficulty of barter exchanges as against money-based exchanges. Barter exchanges necessitate a double coincidence of wants, wherein both parties must possess items desired by the other and mutually consent to trade.

q_en: Who among the following personalities is a professional Kuchipudi Dancer?
e_en: The correct answer is Kaushalya Reddy. Kaushalya Reddy is a renowned figure in the field of Kuchipudi classical dance, showcasing expertise and dedication throughout her career. As a professional performer and educator, she has made significant contributions to the art form, particularly through her role at the Natya Tarangini Institute of Kuchipudi Dance in New Delhi.

q_en: Which region has the maximum concentration of Iron and Steel industries?
e_en: The correct answer is Chota Nagpur Plateau. The Chota Nagpur plateau stands out as the hub of iron and steel industries in India, primarily due to its abundant reserves of high-grade hematite iron ore found in places like Noamundi, Gua, Kolhan, Dharwar, and Budabaru. This region also boasts extensive coal deposits, further bolstering its appeal for iron and steel production. Most of the iron and steel plants are strategically situated acro

q_en: Who among the following has been accused of committing the judicial murder of Raja Nand Kumar?
e_en: The correct answer is Warren Hastings. q_en: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding the Coriolis force?

It is absent at the equator.
Deflection is less when the speed of wind is high.

e_en: The correct answer is Deflection is less when the wind is high. The Coriolis force is an apparent force caused by the Earth's rotation. q_en: Jamshedi Navroz is a festival of _________ community.

Parsis observe this day by cleaning their homes, wearing new clothes, and preparing special meals. The celebrations often include visiting the fire temple to offer prayers and seek blessings.

q_en: The Yakshagana is the dance-drama primarily associated with which of the following states?

The themes of Yakshagana are usually drawn from Hindu epics such as the Ramayana, Mahabharata, and Puranas.

e_en: The correct answer is Sikkim Sikkim recorded the least population according to the Census of India 2011. iii. The Five-Year planning model in India was borrowed from Russia.

The Five-Year planning model in India was inspired by the planning model of the Soviet Union (Russia). The PC Mahalanobis model was actually used for the Second Five-Year Plan, not the first.

q_en: Dussehra festival is celebrated in which of the following Hindu months?

The festival signifies the triumph of good over evil and is celebrated with great enthusiasm across India. In some regions, it is also known as Vijayadashami. The celebration includes the burning of effigies of Ravana, symbolizing the destruction of evil.

q_en: Which country’s national game is Chinlone (Caneball)?

Chinlone is a combination of sport and dance, where players pass a ball made of rattan using their feet, knees, and heads. The game is typically played in a circle with teams or individually, focusing on skill and grace rather than competition. It is an integral part of Myanmar's culture and is often played during festivals and traditional events.

q_en: The Atal Tunnel has been built by Border Road Organisation at an altitude of 3000 metres. Which places are connected by this tunnel?
e_en: The correct answer is Manali to Lahaul-Spiti The Atal Tunnel is a highway tunnel built under the Rohtang Pass in the eastern Pir Panjal range of the Himalayas on the Leh-Manali Highway. It connects Manali to Lahaul-Spiti valley throughout the year, which was previously cut off for about six months due to heavy snowfall. The tunnel is named after former Indian Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee and is one of the longest tunnels above 10,000 feet in the world.

q_en: Where is the renowned Bhatkhande music institute located?
e_en: The correct answer is Lucknow. Bhatkhande Music Institute is located in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, it is one of the prominent institutions for music education in India. The institute was founded by the renowned musicologist Pandit Vishnu Digambar Paluskar and is named after Pandit Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande, a key figure in Indian classical music. It offers courses in various forms of Indian classical music, including Hindustani and Carnatic styles.

q_en: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about the Music of India?
o_en: Tala is a cyclic arrangement of time units.
The musical instrument Kamaicha is majorly used by the ‘Manganiar’ Community of Manipur as a popular accompaniment to their songs

The sruti is a unit of measure or small difference between the various consecutive pitches within a grama or a scale.

The Manganiar community is known for its folk music and often uses the Kamaicha in their performances, but the community of Manipur is more associated with instruments like the pena and dholak.

q_en: In which year did the Bhopal gas tragedy occur?
e_en: The correct answer is 1984 Bhopal Gas Tragedy: It happened on December 3, 1984. It was happened due to leakage of Methyl Isocyanate (CH3NCO) from the pesticide plant of Union Carbide (now Dow Chemicals), an MNC, in Madhya Pradesh capital Bhopal. q_en: The Himalayas' outermost range is called __________.
e_en: The correct answer is option Shivalik. Shivalik range ​The Shivalik Range, also known as the outer Himalayas, is the outermost range of the Himalayas. It features a series of parallel or converging ranges separated by deep valleys, creating a highly dissected topography. The Shivaliks run for 2,400 km from the Potwar Plateau to the Brahmaputra valley, with altitudes ranging from 600 to 1500 meters. The southern slopes are steep, while the northern slopes are gentler.

q_en: Rukmini Devi Arundale is associated with which art form?
e_en: The correct answer is Dance Rukmini Devi Arundale was a prominent figure in Indian culture, known primarily for her contributions to classical Indian dance, particularly Bharatanatyam. She established the Kalakshetra Academy in Chennai, which is renowned worldwide for its training in Bharatanatyam and other classical arts. While she was not a professional painter, Rukmini Devi Arundale had a keen interest in art and engaged in various artistic pursuits.

q_en: Which revolutionary organisation was established at Feroz Shah Kotla in New Delhi in 1928?
e_en: The correct answer is the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association. Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA): Hindustan Republic Association at a historic meeting in the ruins of Ferozshah Kotla in Delhi was converted into Hindustan Socialist Republican Association in September 1928. q_en: In 1812, who described the hypothesis that equal volumes of different gases contain an equal number of molecules?
e_en: The correct answer is Amedeo Avogadro. Equal volumes of different gases containing an equal number of molecules were described by Avogadro. This concept is known as Avogadro's Law. Amedeo Avogadro was an Italian scientist whose work laid the foundation for molecular theory and stoichiometry in chemistry.

q_en:
Which of the following statements about Akbar are true?

2 He defeated and merged the state of Bijapur in his empire.
3 He made Fatehpur Sikri his capital.
e_en: The correct answer is Only 1 and 3. Akbar introduced the Mansabdari system to organize the military and administration. Akbar is known for his policy of religious tolerance and founded the Din-i-Ilahi to promote unity among different religions. He expanded the Mughal Empire significantly through both diplomacy and warfare, including the conquest of Gujarat and Bengal.

q_en: In which of the following states is the Sanchi Stupa UNESCO world heritage site located?
e_en: The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh. The Sanchi Stupa was commissioned by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE and is one of the oldest stone structures in India. The Stupa is known for its hemispherical dome that houses relics of Buddha and is surrounded by ornate gateways (Toranas) symbolizing love, peace, trust, and courage.

q_en: Which of the following persons was appointed Chairman of the Second National Judicial Pay Commission?
e_en: The correct answer is Justice PV Reddi. Justice P.V. Reddi was appointed as the Chairman of the Second National Judicial Pay Commission in 2010 to examine and recommend pay structures for judges in the higher judiciary. The Commission's primary objective was to assess the working conditions, remuneration, and service conditions of judges, including those in the Supreme Court and High Courts, to ensure adequate compensation and facilities.

q_en: National Sports Day is celebrated on the birthday of _______.
e_en: The correct answer is Major Dhyan Chand. Major Dhyan Chand (29 August 1905 – 3 December 1979) was an Indian field hockey player widely regarded as the greatest in the history of the sport. He was known for his extraordinary goal-scoring feats, in addition to earning three Olympic gold medals, in 1928, 1932, and 1936, during an era where India dominated field hockey. Known as The Wizard or The Magician of hockey for his superb ball control.

q_en: A constellation of the northern sky easily recognised by a group of five bright stars forming a slightly irregular ‘W’ is called:
e_en: The correct answer is Cassiopeia. Cassiopeia A is a supernova remnant. It is notable for being the brightest astronomical radio source in the sky. It is the strongest radio source in the sky outside the solar system and was one of the first radio sources to be discovered, in 1947. The five brightest stars of Cassiopeia – Alpha, Beta, Gamma, Delta, and Epsilon Cassiopeiae – form the characteristic W-shaped asterism.

q_en: Which of the following states is famous for celebrating the festival of Vijaya Dashami, which marks the end of Durga Puja?
e_en: The correct answer is West Bengal. Vijaya Dashami marks the end of Durga Puja, symbolizing the victory of Goddess Durga over the buffalo demon Mahishasura, representing the triumph of good over evil. On this day, idols of Goddess Durga are taken for immersion (Visarjan) in rivers or water bodies, signifying her return to Mount Kailash.

q_en: Which of the following is NOT a characteristics of the National Investment and Manufacturing Zones (NIMZs) of India?

NIMZs are developed to promote manufacturing and attract investment in the industrial sector, as part of the National Manufacturing Policy, 2011. Each NIMZ is a large industrial cluster, spread over a minimum of 5,000 hectares, with integrated infrastructure, including roads, water, and power supply.

q_en: In which year was the National Human Rights Commission established in India?
e_en: The correct answer is 1993. The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) was established in India on 12 October 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. Its main purpose is to protect and promote human rights, including civil, political, economic, social, and cultural rights guaranteed by the Constitution and international treaties.
