q_en: If cos² θ – sin² θ – 3cosθ + 2 = 0, 0° < θ < 90°, then what is the value of 4 cosecθ + cotθ?
e_en: Given: cos² θ – sin² θ – 3cosθ + 2 = 0 ⇒ cos² θ – (1 – cos² θ) – 3cos θ + 2 = 0 ⇒ cos² θ – 1 + cos² θ – 3cos θ + 2 = 0 ⇒ 2cos² θ – 3cos θ + 1 = 0 ⇒ 2cos² θ – 2cosθ – cos θ + 1 = 0 ⇒ 2cosθ (cos θ – 1) – 1(cos θ – 1) = 0 ⇒ (2 cos θ – 1)(cos θ – 1) = 0 ⇒ cos θ = ½ or cos θ = 1 Cos θ = 1 is not possible as θ < 90° ⇒ cos θ = ½ ⇒ θ = 60° Now, 4 cosec θ + cot θ = 4 cosec60° + cot60° ⇒ 4 cosec θ + cot θ = 4 × 2/√ 3 + 1/√ 3 = 9/√ 3 = 3√

q_en: The simple interest on a certain sum for 3 ½ years at 10% per annum is Rs. 2,940. What will be the compound interest on the same sum for 2 ½ years at the same rate when interest is compounded yearly (nearest to rupee)?
e_en: S.I. = PRT/100 ⇒ 2940 = (P × 10 × 7/2)/100 ⇒ P = Rs. 8400 Now, C.I. on Rs.8400 for first year at 10% rate of interest = 10/100 × 8400 = Rs. 840 ⇒ Principal for second year = 8400 + 840 = Rs. 9240 C.I. at 10% for second year = 10/100 × 9240 = Rs. 924 ⇒ Principal for last 6 months = 8400 + 840 + 924 = Rs. 10164 As we have to calculate interest for six months, rate of interest = 10/2 = 5% C.I.

q_en: The ratio of the combined target production of AC Machines In January and April to that of the combined actual production of AC Machine in March and April was:
e_en: Combined target production of AC Machines In January and April = 60000 + 90000 = 150000 Combined actual production of AC Machine in March and April = 100000 + 80000 = 180000 ∴ The ratio of the combined target production of AC Machines In January and April to that of the combined actual production of AC Machine in March and April is = 150000 : 180000 = 5 : 6

q_en: The actual production of AC Machines in April was what percentage more than the average target production of AC Machines over five months?
e_en: The average target production of AC Machines over five months = (60 + 30 + 80 + 90 + 100)/5 = 72 The actual production of AC machines in April exceeds the average target production of AC Machines over five months by 80 – 72 = 8 ⇒ 8/72 × 100 = 100/9 = 11 1/9% ∴ The actual production of AC machines in April exceeds the average target production of AC Machines over five months by 11 1/9%

q_en: The total target production of AC Machines in February, April and May was what percentage less than the total actual production of AC Machines over all the five months (correct to one decimal place)?
e_en: The total target production of AC Machines in February, April and May = 30 + 90 + 100 = 220 The total actual production of AC Machines over all the five months = 70 + 50 + 100 + 80 + 120 = 420 Hence, (420 - 220)/420 × 100 = 47.6% ∴ The total target production of AC Machines in February, April and May was what 47.6% less than the total actual production of AC Machines over all the five months

q_en: In which month the actual production of AC Machines was 25% more than the target production?
e_en: In January, (70 – 60)/60 × 100 = 16.66% In February, (50 – 30)/30 × 100 = 66.66% In March, (100 – 80)/80 × 100 = 25% ∴ In March the actual production of AC Machines was 25% more than the target.

q_en: A is 20% more than B, B is 25% more than C, C is 60% less than D and D is 20% more than E. Based on the above information, which of the following is true?
e_en: Let E = 100 ⇒ D = (100 + 20)/100 × 100 = 120 ⇒ C = (100 – 60)/100 × 120 = 48 ⇒ B = (100 + 25)/100 × 48 = 60 ⇒ A = (100 + 20)/100 × 60 = 72 Checking option A: (72 – 48)/72 × 100 = 33.33% Hence option A is incorrect. Checking option B: (120 – 72)/120 × 100 = 40% Hence option B is correct Checking option C: (100 – 72)/72 × 100 = 38.88% Hence option C is incorrect. Checking option D: It can be clearly seen that D is greater than B. Hence option D is incorrect.

q_en: Two trains of same length are running on parallel tracks in the same direction at 54 km/h and 42 km/h respectively. The faster train passes the other train in 60 seconds. What is the length (in metres) of each train?
e_en: Relative speed of fastest train = 54 – 42 = 12 km/hr = 12 × 5/18 = 10/3 m/s. Let the length of the train be x metre. As both the trains are running on parallel tracks in same direction, the distance covered by the fastest train will be x + x = 2x We have, Distance/Time = Speed 2x/60 = 10/3 x = 100 metre ∴ The length of each train = 100 metre.

q_en: If a² + 4b² + 49c² + 18 = 2 (2b + 28c – a), then the value of (3a + 2b + 7c) is:
A ΔABC, D and E are the points on sides AB and AC, respectively, such that DE || BC. If DE : BC is 3 : 5, then (Area of ΔADE): (Area of quadrilateral DECB) is:
e_en: By Thales’ intercept theorem: DE/BC = AD/AB = AE/AC = 3/5 Hence ratio of sides of ADE and ABC = 3 : 5 ⇒ Ratio of sides of ADE and ABC = 3² : 5² = 9 : 25 Let the area of ADE = 9x and area of ABC = 25x Area of trapezium DECB = Area of ABC – Area of ABC = 25x – 9x = 16x ∴ Area of ΔADE : Area of quadrilateral DECB = 9x : 16x = 9 : 16

q_en: The volume of a right circular cone is 924 cm³. If its height is 18 cm, then the area of its base (in cm²) is:
e_en: Correct answer: 154.

q_en: The ratio of the incomes of A and B is 2 : 3 and that of their expenditure is 1 : 2. If 90% of B’s expenditure is equal to the income of A, then what is the ratio of the savings of A and B?
e_en: Let the income of A be 2x and income of B be 3x and their expenditure be y and 2y respectively. 90% of B’s expenditure is equal to the income of A. ⇒ 90/100 × 2y = 2x ⇒ 9y = 10x ⇒ y = 10x/9 Savings of A = Income – Expenditure = 2x – y = 2x – 10x/9 = 8x/9 Savings of B = Income – Expenditure = 3x – 2y = 3x – 2 × 10x/9 = 7x/9 ∴ The ratio of the savings of A and B = 8x/9 : 7x/9 = 8 : 7

q_en: After allowing a discount of 10% on the marked price of an article, it is sold for Rs. 360. Had the discount not been given, the profit would have been 25%. What is the cost price of the article?
e_en: MP × 90/100 = 360 MP = 400 Had the discount not been given the selling price would have been MP. ⇒ CP × 125/100 = 400 ∴ CP = 320

q_en: There are 90 students in a class, out of which 70% are from village A and others are from village B. The average score of students from village B in a test is 20% more than that from village A. If the average score of all the students is 53, then what is the average score of the students from village B?
e_en: Students from village A = 70/100 × 90 = 63 Students from village B = 90-63 = 27 Let the average score of students from village A = x ⇒ Average score of students from village B = 1.2 x ⇒ Average score of all the students = [63 x + 27(1.2 x)]/90 = 53 ⇒ x = 50 and 1.2 x = 1.2 × 50 = 60 ∴ The average score of the students from village B = 60

q_en: The ratio of speeds of A and B is 3 : 5. If A takes 24 minutes more than B to cover a certain distance, then how much time (in minutes) will B take to cover the same distance?
e_en: Given: The ratio of speeds of A and B = 3 : 5 Time taken by A to cover a distance = 24 minutes more than B Formula used: Speed = Distance traveled/Time taken If Distance → Constant, then Speed ∝ 1/time Calculation: Ratio of speeds of A and B = 3 : 5 ⇒ Ratio of time of A and B = 5 : 3 Let time taken by A and B be 5x and 3x respectively. Difference in time taken by A and B = 5x – 3x = 2x = 24 mins. ⇒ x = 12 Time taken by B to cover the same distance = 3x = 3 × 12 = 36 mins

q_en: The average number of students (per year), enrolled in B during 2015, 2016 and 2018 is more by what percentage than the number of students enrolled in A during 2017?
e_en: Calculation: The average number of students enrolled in B during 2015, 2016, and 2018 ⇒ (360 + 375 + 225)/3 = 320 The number of students enrolled in A during 2017 = 250 Required percentage = (320 – 250)/250 × 100 = 28%

q_en: The total number of students enrolled in A during 2014, 2016 and 2018 is what percentage (correct to one decimal place) of the total number of students enrolled in B during the period of five years?
e_en: Calculation: The total number of students enrolled in A during 2014, 2016, and 2018 ⇒ 160 + 300 + 260 = 720 The total number of students enrolled in B during the period of five years ⇒ 225 + 360 + 375 + 325 + 225 = 1510 Required percentage = 720/1510 × 100 = 47.7%

q_en: What is the ratio of the total number of students enrolled in A during 2015 and 2018 to the total number of students enrolled in B during 2014 and 2016?
e_en: Calculation: The total number of students enrolled in A during 2015 and 2018 ⇒ 280 + 260 = 540 The total number of students enrolled in B during 2014 and 2016 ⇒ 225 + 375 = 600 ∴ Required ratio = 540 : 600 = 9 : 10

q_en: In which year the number of students enrolled in B is x% more, where 25 < x < 30, than the number of students enrolled in A in the same year?
e_en: Calculation: For year 2015: The number of students enrolled in B is more than the number of students enrolled in A by 360 – 280 = 80 Percent by which the number of students in B exceeds by A = 80/280 × 100 = 28.57% For year 2017: The number of students enrolled in B is more than the number of students enrolled in A by 325 – 250 = 75 Percent by which the number of students in B exceeds by A = 75/250 × 100 = 30% For year 2016: The number of students enrolled in B is more than t…

q_en: If x + 1/x = 7, then x³ + 1/x³ is equal to:
e_en: Correct answer: 322.

q_en: If 250√2 x³ – 5√5 y³ = (5√2 x - √5 y) × (Ax² + Bxy + Cy²), then the value of A + C - √10 B is:
e_en: Given: 250√2 x3 – 5√5 y3 = (5√2 x - √5 y) × (Ax2 + Bxy + Cy2) ----(1) Formula used: a³ - b³ = (a - b)(a² + b² + ab) Calculation: Taking L.H.S. of Eq(1) 250√2 x³ – 5√5 y³ ⇒ (5√2 x - √5 y) × [(5√2 x)² + 5√10 xy + (√5 y)²] ⇒ (5√2 x - √5 y) × (50x² + 5√10 xy + 5y²) Equating with R.H.S. (5√2 x - √5 y) × (50x² + 5√10 xy + 5y²) = (5√2 x - √5 y) × (Ax² + Bxy + Cy²) A = 50, B = 5√10, C = 5 A + C - √10 B = 50 + 5 – 50 ∴ A + C - √10 B = 5

q_en: Two numbers A and B are in the ratio 5 : 2, If 4 is added to each number then this ratio becomes 9 : 4. If 5 is subtracted from each of the original number, then the ratio of A and B will be:
e_en: Given: The ratio of two numbers A and B = 5 : 2 Ratio of two numbers if 4 is added to it = 9 : 4 Calculation: Let the two numbers be 5x and 2x When 4 is added to each number, (5x + 4)/(2x + 4) = 9/4 ⇒ 4(5x + 4) = 9(2x + 4) ⇒ 20x + 16 = 18x + 36 ⇒ 20x – 18x = 36 – 16 ⇒ 2x = 20 ⇒ x = 10 The original number = 5x = 50 and 2x = 20 When 5 is subtracted from each number, the ratio ⇒ (50 - 5) : (20 - 5) = 45 : 15 = 3 : 1

q_en: A certain sum amounts to Rs. 29282 in 4 years at 10% per annum, when the interest is compounded annually. What is the simple interest on the same sum for same time at the same rate?
e_en: Given: Amount = Rs. 29282 Rate = 10% per annum Time = 4 years Formula used: For compound interest, A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ For Simple Interest S.I. = (P × R × T)/100 Where, A = Amount P = Principal r = rate of interest n = time period in years Calculation: ⇒ 29282 = P(1 + 10/100)⁴ ⇒ 29282 = P(11/10)⁴ ⇒ P = 29282 × 10/11 × 10/11 × 10/11 × 10/11 ⇒ P = Rs. 20000 Now, S.I. = PRT/100 ⇒ S.I. = (20000 × 10 × 4)/100 ⇒ S.I. = Rs. 8000

q_en: A rectangle ABCD is inscribed in a circle with centre O. Its diagonal CA is produced to a point E, outside the circle. ED is a tangent to the circle at D. If AC = 2BC, then what is the measure of ∠DEC?
e_en: Correct answer: 30°.

q_en: By selling an article for Rs. 2300, Rekha gains 25%. If she sells it for Rs. 1955, then her loss/gain percent is:
e_en: Given: S.P. of an article = Rs. 2300 Gain% = 25% Formula used: C.P. = (S.P. × 100)/(100 + gain%) Loss % = (Loss/C.P.) × 100% Calculation: C.P. of article = 2300 × 100/(100 + 25) = Rs. 1840 If the article is sold for Rs.1955, profit = 1955 – 1840 = 115 ∴ Gain percent = 115/1840 × 100 = 6.25%

q_en: If ΔABC ~ ΔQPR, Area ΔABC : Area ΔPQR = 9 : 16. If AB = 12 cm, BC = 6 cm and AC = 9 cm, then QR is equal to:
e_en: Given: ΔABC ~ ΔQPR Area ΔABC : Area ΔPQR = 9 : 16 Concept used: If two triangles are similar, then the ratio of their areas will be equal to the ratio of the squares of their corresponding sides. ⇒ Area ΔABC : Area ΔPQR = AB²/PQ² Calculation: ⇒ Side ΔABC : Side ΔPQR = √9 : √16 = 3 : 4 ΔABC ~ ΔQPR ⇒ AC/QR = 3/4 ⇒ 9/QR = 3/4 ⇒ QR = 12 cm

q_en:
A wire is in the shape of a rectangle whose sides are in the ratio 7 : 4. It was initially in the shape of a circle of radius, very nearly equal to 31.5 cm. The length of smaller side of the rectangle is:
Take π = 22/7
e_en: Given: Ratio of sides of rectangle = 7 : 4 Circumference of wire = 31.5 cm Formula used: Circumference of circle = 2πr Perimeter of rectangle = 2(l + b) Calculation: Circumference of circle = 2 × 22/7 × 31.5 ⇒ 198 cm Let the length and breadth of rectangle be 7x and 4x respectively Perimeter of rectangle = 2(l + b) = 2(7x + 4x) = 22x Now, Circumference of circle = perimeter of rectangle (as the wire is same) ⇒ 198 = 22x ⇒ x = 9 ∴ The length of smaller side = 4x = 4 × 9 = 36 c…

q_en: A and B together can do a piece of work in 10 days, B and C together can do it in 15 days while C and A together can do it in 20 days. They work together for 8 days. C alone will complete the remaining work in:
e_en: 2(A + B + C) = 6 + 4 + 3 ⇒ 2(A + B + C) = 13 ⇒ A + B + C = 6.5 If A, B and C work together for 8 days, the work done = 8 × 6.5 = 52 units Remaining work = 60 – 52 = 8 units Efficiency of C = Efficiency of (A + B + C) – Efficiency of (A + B) ⇒ Efficiency of C = 6.5 – 6 = 0.5 ∴ The remaining work will be completed by C in 8/0.5 = 16 days

q_en: A man gets a discount of 30% and then 20% on his food bill. How much equivalent single discount does he get?
e_en: Given: The successive discount are 30% and 20%. Formula used: Equivalent single discount = X + Y - (XY)/100 Where, X = First discount Y = Second discount Calculation: Equivalent single discount = X + Y - (XY)/100 ⇒ 30 + 20 – (30 × 20)/100 ⇒ 50 – 6 ⇒ 44% ∴ Equivalent single discount is 44%.

q_en: In a circle with centre O, ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral with AB as a diameter of the circle. AD and BC produced to meet at E such that AE = BE. If ∠CED = 70°, then what is the measure of ∠COD?
e_en: Given: AE = BE ⇒ ΔAEB is an isosceles triangle. ⇒ ∠EAB = ∠EBA In ΔAEB, ∠AEB + ∠EAB + ∠EBA = 180° ⇒ 70° + 2∠EAB = 180° ⇒ 2∠EAB = 110° ⇒ ∠EAB = 55° ⇒ ∠EBA = 55° Now, DO = AO = OC = OB = radius In ΔADO, AO = OD ⇒ ∠DAO = ∠ADO = 55° ⇒ ∠DOA = 180° - 55° - 55° = 70° In ΔOCB OC = OB ⇒ ∠CBO = ∠BCO = 55° ⇒ ∠COB = 180° - 55° - 55° = 70° Now, ∠AOB = 180° ∠COD = 180° - ∠DOA - ∠COB ⇒ ∠COD = 180° - 70° - 70° = 40°

q_en: In triangle ABC, the length of BC is less than twice the length of AB by 2 cm. The length of AC exceeds the length of AB by 10 cm. The perimeter is 32 cm. The length (in cm) of the smallest side of the triangle is:
e_en: Calculation: Let the length of AB = x cm The length of BC = (2x - 2) cm, and the length of AC = (x + 10) cm The perimeter of ΔABC = 32 cm. ⇒ x + 2x - 2 + x + 10 = 32 ⇒ 4x + 8 = 32 ⇒ 4x = 24 ⇒ x = 6 The lengths of the sides of the triangle are: AB = x cm = 6 cm BC = (2x - 2) cm = 10 cm AC = (x + 10) = 16 cm ∴ The length of the smallest side of the triangle is 6 cm.

q_en: A circle is inscribed in a triangle ABC. It touches sides AB, BC, and AC at points P, Q, and R respectively. If BP = 5 cm, CQ = 7 cm and AR = 6 cm, then the perimeter (in cm) of the ΔABC is:
e_en: Given: BP = 5 cm, CQ = 7 cm and AR = 6cm Calculation: The lengths of tangents from a point on a circle are equal. Thus, AP = AR = 6 cm BQ = BP = 5 cm CR = CQ = 7 cm Now, AB = AP + PB = 6 + 5 = 11 cm BC = BQ + QC = 5 + 7 = 12 cm AC = AR + CR = 6 + 7 = 13 cm The perimeter of ΔABC = AB + BC + AC ∴ The perimeter of ΔABC = 11 + 12 + 13 = 36 cm

q_en: A man bought 2 articles for Rs. 4158 each. He sold one article at a 15% loss. Then at what percent profit the other article should be sold so that no profit/loss percentage is earned?
e_en: Calculation: The total cost price of both the articles = 2 × 4158 = Rs. 8316 The selling price of the article sold at 15% loss = 4158 × [(100 - 15)/100] = Rs. 3534.3 For no profit/loss, the other article must be sold for = 8316 - 3534.3 = Rs. 4781.7 Hence, the profit on the other article = 4781.7 - 4158 = Rs. 623.7 ∴ Profit percent on the other article = 623.7/4158 × 100 = 15%

q_en: If a 10 - digit number 7220x558y2 is divisible by 88, then the value of (5x + 5y) is:
e_en: Calculation: For a number to be divisible be 88, it should be divisible by 11 and 8. For a number to be divisible by 8, the last three digits of the number should be divisible by 8. Putting y = 3, the last 3 digits become 832, which is divisible by 8. For a number to be divisible by 11, the difference of the sum of the alternate numbers should be zero or multiple of 11. ⇒ The difference of (7 + 2 + x + 5 + 3) and (2 + 0 + 5 + 8 + 2) should be zero or multiple of 11.

q_en: A, B and C can complete a piece of work in 4, 20 and 60 days respectively. Working together, they can complete the same work in how many days?
e_en: Correct answer: 60/19.

q_en: Two numbers are in the ratio 7 : 5, on diminishing each of them by 40, the ratio becomes 27 : 17. The difference between the number is:
e_en: Calculation: Let the two numbers be 7x and 5x. According to the question: (7x - 40)/(5x - 40) = 27/17 ⇒ 119x - 680 = 135x - 1080 ⇒ 16x = 400 ⇒ x = 25 ∴ The difference between numbers = 7x - 5x = 2x = 2 × 25 = 50

q_en: If sec θ = 4x and tan θ= 4/x, (x ≠ 0) then the value of 8(x² - 1/x²) is:
e_en: We have, sec²θ - tan²θ = 1 ⇒ (4x)² - (4/x)² = 1 ⇒ 16x² - 16/x² = 1 ⇒ 16(x² - 1/x²) = 1 ⇒ 8(x² - 1/x²) = 1/2

q_en: If (1)/({1 - sintheta )} + (1)/({1 + sintheta )} = 4secθ, 0°<θ<90°, then the value of (3 cot θ + cosec θ) is:
e_en: Correct answer: 5√3/3.

q_en: If cos x = - 1/2 and π < x < 3π/2, then the value of 4tan²x + 3cosec²x is:
e_en: As π < x < 3π/2, x lies in third quadrant. cos x = - 1/2 ⇒ x = 240° 4tan²x + 3cosec²x ⇒ 4tan²(240°) + 3cosec²(240°) ⇒ 4tan²(180° + 60°) + 3cosec²(180° + 60°) ⇒ 4tan²60° + 3(-cosec 60°)² ⇒ 4 × (√3)² + 3 × (-2/√3)² ⇒ 4 × 3 + 3 × 4/3 ⇒ 16

q_en: Out of given four different numbers, the average of the first three numbers is four times the fourth number and the average of all the four numbers is 52. What is the average of the first three numbers?
e_en: Given: Average of 1st three numbers = 4 × fourth no. Average of all the four numbers = 52 Formula used: Average = Sum of observation/no. of observation

q_en: The ratio of the areas of two triangles ABC and PQR is 3 ∶ 5 and the ratio of their heights is 5 : 3. The ratio of the bases of triangle ABC to that of triangle PQR is:
e_en: Calculation: Let the height and base of ΔABC be H and B respectively, and the height and base of ΔPQR be h and b respectively. Area of ΔABC / Area of ΔPQR = (B × H) / (b × h) ⇒ 3 / 5 = 5B / 3b ⇒ B / b = 9 / 25 ∴ The ratio of the bases of triangle ABC to that of triangle PQR is 9 : 25.

q_en: In a ΔABC, the bisectors of ∠B and ∠C meet at point O within the triangle. If ∠A = 116°, then the measure of ∠BOC is:
e_en: Calculation: We have, ∠BOC = 90° + ½ ∠A ⇒ ∠BOC = 90° + ½ (116°) ⇒ ∠BOC = 90° + 58 ∴ ∠BOC = 148°

q_en: If 5∛x + 12∛x = 13∛x, then the value of x is:
e_en: Calculation: By hit and trial, putting x = 8 5∛x + 12∛x = 13∛x ⇒ 5∛⁸ + 12∛⁸ = 13∛⁸ ⇒ 5² + 12² = 13² ⇒ 25 + 144 = 169 ⇒ 169 = 169 ⇒ L.H.S = R.H.S ∴ The value of x = 8.

q_en: If one of the angles of a triangle is 64°, then the angle between the bisectors of the other two interior angles is:
e_en: Given: One angle of a triangle = 64° Concept used: If the ∠BIC is an angle at incentre of the triangle so value of ∠BIC = 90° + ∠BAC/2 Calculations: In ΔABC, ∠ABC + ∠ACB + ∠BAC = 180° ⇒ ∠ABC + 2∠ICB + 2∠IBC = 180° ⇒ ∠ICB + ∠IBC = (180° – 64°)/2 = 58° Now, in ΔBIC, ∠ICB + ∠IBC + ∠BIC = 180° ⇒ 58° + ∠BIC = 180° ⇒ ∠BIC = 180° – 58° = 122° ∴ The value of ∠BIC is 122° Short trick∶ We know the identity, ∠BIC = 90° + ∠A/2 ⇒ 90° + 64°/2 = 90° + 32° ⇒ 122° ∴ The value of ∠BIC is 122°

q_en: The price of a commodity is increased by 36% and the quantity purchased is decreased by 30%. What is the percentage increase/decrease in the amount spent on the commodity?
e_en: Given: Increase % in price of commodity = 36% Decrease in quantity = 30% Concept used: Expenditure = Price of commodity × Quantity Calculation: Let the price of a commodity be Rs. 100/unit and the quantity purchased be 10 units ⇒ Amount spent = 100 × 10 = Rs.

q_en: The ratio between the speeds of two trains is 5 ∶ 7. If the first train covers 300 km in 3 hours, then the speed (in km/h) of the second train is:
e_en: Calculation: Let the speed of the first train be 5x and the speed of the second train be 7x. Speed of the first train = Distance / Time = 300/3 = 100 km/hr According to the question: 5x = 100 ⇒ x = 20 ∴ The speed of the second train = 7x = 7 × 20 = 140 km/hr.

q_en: The marked price of an article is Rs. 400. After allowing a discount of 20% on the marked price, a shopkeeper makes a profit of Rs. 32. His gain percent is:
e_en: Given: M.P. of an article = Rs. 400 Discount % = 20% Profit = Rs. 32 Formula used: S.P. = M.P. × (100 - Discount%)/100 Profit = S.P. - C.P. Profit % = Profit/C.P. × 100 Calculation: S.P = M.P. × 80/100 ⇒ 400 × 80/100 ⇒ Rs. 320 C.P. = S.P. – Profit ⇒ 320 – 32 ⇒ Rs. 288 ∴ Gain percentage = 32/288 × 100 = 11.11%

q_en: A person purchased a vehicle for Rs. 5,90,828 and sold it for Rs. 6,52,920. What is the profit percent he earned on this vehicle (correct to two decimal places)?
e_en: The formula used: Profit = Selling Price - Cost Price Calculation: Profit = 652920 - 590828 = Rs. 62092 ⇒ Profit percentage = 62092/590828 × 100 = 10.50%

q_en: The average age of four brothers is 15 years. If their father is included, the average is increased by 5 years. The age of the father (in years) is:
e_en: Given: The average age of four brothers = 15 years Calculation: The total age of four brothers = 15 × 4 = 60 years If their father’s age is included, the average age is increased by 5 years. New average = 15 + 5 = 20 years ⇒ The total age of four brothers and their father = 20 × 5 = 100 years ∴ The age of father = 100 - 60 = 40 years.

q_en: A number is increased by 30%, then decreased by 30%, then further decreased by 30%. What is the net increase/decrease percent in the number (correct to the nearest integer)?
e_en: Calculation: Let the number be 100x. When the number is increased by 30%, then decreased by 30%, then further decreased by 30%, it becomes: 100x × [(100 + 30)/100] × [(100 - 30)/100] × [(100 - 30)/100] ⇒ 100 × (130/100) × (70/100) × (70/100) ⇒ 63.7x Decrease in Number = 100x - 63.7x = 36.3x ∴ Percentage decrease in number = 100 × (36.3x/100x) = 36.3% ≈ 36%

q_en: There was 25% off on the shirt. A lady bought that shirt and got an additional 20% discount for paying in cash and a further 10% discount for being a loyal customer. She paid Rs. 324. What was the price tag (in Rs.) on the shirt?
e_en: Calculation: Let the price tag on the shirt be 100x. According to the question: 100x × (100 - 25)/100 × (100 - 20)/100 × (100 - 10)/100 = 324 ⇒ 100x × 75/100 × 80/100 × 90/100 = 324 ⇒ 100x = 324 × 100/75 × 100/80 × 100/90 ⇒ 100x = 600 ∴ The price tag on the shirt was Rs. 600

q_en: By how much quantity is the average sale per month from B more or less than that from C?
e_en: Calculation: The total sale from B of all the months = 9000 + 7000 + 9000 + 11000 = 36000 The average sale from B of all the months = 36000/4 = 9000 The total sale from C of all the months = 10000 + 5000 + 8000 + 9000 = 32000 The average sale from C of all the months = 32000/4 = 8000 kg Difference of the average sale from B and C = 9000 – 8000 = 1000 kg ∴ The average sale per month from B is 1000 kg more than that from C

q_en: What is the average sale per month by A during Jan-Mar, 2018?
e_en: Calculation: The average sale by A during Jan – Mar,2018 = (8000 + 6000 + 8000)/3 = 7333.33 kg ∴ The correct answer is 7333.33 kg

q_en: Arrange the ratio of sales from B to that from A and C, taken together, month wise in ascending order.
e_en: Calculation: Ratio of sales from B to that from A and C in Jan = 9/(8 + 10) = 9/18 = 0.5 Ratio of sales from B to that from A and C in Feb = 7/(6 + 5) = 7/11 = 0.63 Ratio of sales from B to that from A and C in Mar = 9/(8 + 8) = 9/16 = 0.56 Ratio of sales from B to that from A and C in Apr = 11/(9 + 9) = 11/18 = 0.61 ∴ Arranging them in ascending order: Jan, Mar, Apr, Feb

q_en: What is the ratio of rate of growth in sales from B to the rate of growth in sales from C in Mar 2018 with reference to its previous month?
e_en: Calculation: The rate of growth in sales from B in March 2018 with reference to its previous month = (9 – 7)/7 = 2/7 The rate of growth in sales from C in March 2018 with reference to its previous month = (8 – 5)/5 = 3/5 The ratio of rate of growth in sales from B to the rate of growth in sales from C in Mar 2018 with reference to its previous month = 2/7 : 3/5 = 10 : 21 ∴ The correct answer is 10 : 21.

q_en:
The circumcentre, incentre, orthocentre and the centroid of a triangle are one and the same point. The triangle must be:
(a) isosceles (b) right-angled (c) right-angled isosceles (d) equilateral
e_en: Calculation: In an equilateral triangle, the circumcentre, incentre, orthocentre and the centroid of a triangle are one and the same point. The correct option is option B.

q_en: Two items are sold for Rs. 18,602 each. On one item there has been a gain of 31% and on the second item a loss of 29%. What was the overall loss or gain in the transaction?
e_en: Given: Two items are sold for Rs. 18,602 each Calculation: The cost price of the item sold at 31% gain = 18602 × 100/(100 + 31) = Rs. 14200 The cost price of the item sold at 29% loss = 18602 × 100/(100 – 29) = Rs. 26200 ⇒ The total cost price of both the items = 14200 + 26200 = Rs. 40400 The total selling price of both the items = 18602 + 18602 = Rs. 37204 Loss = Total cost price – Total selling price ⇒ 40400 – 37204 ⇒ Rs.

q_en: For θ being an acute angle, it is given that, 3 (cosec² θ + cot² θ) = 5. Then θ is equal to:
e_en: Calculation: 3 × (cosec² θ + cot² θ) = 5 ⇒ 3( 1 + cot² θ + cot² θ ) = 5 (∵ cosec² θ – cot² θ = 1) ⇒ 3( 1 + 2 cot² θ) = 5 ⇒ 3 + 6 cot² θ = 5 ⇒ 6 cot² θ = 2 ⇒ cot² θ = 2/6 ⇒ cot² θ = 1/3 ⇒ cot θ = 1/√3 ⇒ θ = 60° ∴ The correct answer is θ = 60° 8a

q_en: Which among the following increases continuously in the range 0° < θ < 90°?
e_en: Calculation: In the first quadrant, i.e. 0° < θ < 90°, sinθ, tanθ and secθ are increasing functions and cosθ, cotθ and cosecθ are decreasing functions. ∴ The correct answer is tanθ.

q_en: The seven digit number 78x1y68 is divisible by 88. The value of (x + y) is:
e_en: Given: The seven-digit number 78x1y68 is divisible by 88. Concept used: (i) For a number to be divisible by 88, it should be divisible by 8 and 11. (ii) Divisibility Rule of 11: For a number to be divisible by 11, the difference between the sum of digits at even places to the sum of digits at odd places should be zero or multiple of 11 Calculations: Checking divisibility by 11, ⇒ The difference of (7 + x + y + 8) and (8 + 1 + 6) should be zero or multiple of 11.

q_en: If (3x + 1)³ + (x - 3)³ + (2x - 4)³ = 3 (3x + 1) (x - 3) (2x - 4), then x is equal to:
e_en: Given: (3x + 1)³ + (x - 3)³ + (2x - 4)³ = 3 (3x + 1) (x - 3) (2x - 4) Calculation: If a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc, then a + b + c = 0 So, ⇒ (3x + 1) + (x – 3) + (2x – 4) = 0 ⇒ 6x – 6 = 0 ⇒ 6x = 6 ⇒ x = 1 ∴ The correct answer is 1.

q_en: A certain sum invested on compound interest grows to Rs. 8,000 and Rs. 27,000 in three and six years, respectively when the interest is compounded annually, what is the percentage rate of interest?
e_en: Given: Amount for 3 years = 8000 Amount for 6 years = 27000 Formula used: A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ Where, A = Amount P = Principal, r = Rate of interest, n = Time period Calculation: When the sum amounts to Rs.8000 in 3 years: 8000 = P(1 + r/100)³ ----(1) When the sum amounts to Rs.27000 in 6 years: 27000 = P(1 + r/100)⁶ ----(2) Dividing equation (2) by equation (1) 27/8 = (1 + r/100)³ Taking cube root on both the sides 1 + r/100 = 3/2 ⇒ r/100 = 3/2 – 1 ⇒ r/100 = 1/2 ⇒ r = 50% ∴ Rat…

q_en: If I travel by bus, I reach my office 15 min late, and if I travel by car, I reach 10 min early. If the distance between my home and my office is 25 km, then the difference of the reciprocals of average speeds of the bus and the car, in second per metre is:
e_en: Calculation: Difference in time = 15 + 10 = 25 min = 1500 second Distance = 25 km = 25000 m Let the speed of bus be B m/s and the speed of car be C m/s ⇒ 25000/B – 25000/C = 1500 ⇒ 25000(1/B – 1/C) = 1500 ⇒ 1/B – 1/C = 1500/25000 = 3/50 ∴ The difference of the reciprocals of average speeds of the bus and the car is 3/50 seconds per metre.

q_en: In a stadium an athlete is running on a circular path with uniform speed during a practice session. The angle covered by him during one second is found to be 10° by coach observing him from the centre of the circular track. What would be the measure of angle (in degree) described by the athlete by an observer standing on the circle?
o_en: it depends on the exact position of the observer on the circle
e_en: Calculation: Let the observer stand at point A on the circle. The angle subtended by an arc at any point on the major segment is half of the angle subtended by the arc at the centre of the circle. ⇒ ∠BAC = ½ ∠BOC = 10°/2 = 5° ∴ The measure of angle described by the athlete by an observer standing on the circle is 5°

q_en: For an examination of a practical based subject, the total marks is 100. The break-up for theory, practical, project and viva voce is 40%, 30%, 20%, 10%. A candidate scored 80% in theory, 70% in practical, 60% in project and 50% in viva voce. What was her aggregate percentage?
e_en: Calculation: Marks scored by the student in theory = 40 × 80/100 = 32 Marks scored by the student in practical = 30 × 70/100 = 21 Marks scored by the student in project = 20 × 60/100 = 12 Marks scored by the student in viva = 10 × 50/100 = 5 Total marks scored by the student = 32 + 21 + 12 + 5 = 70 The aggregate percentage = 70/100 × 100 = 70% ∴ The correct answer is 70%

During a practice session in a stadium an athlete runs along a circular track and her performance is observed by her coach standing at point on the circle and also by her physiotherapist standing at the centre of the circle. The coach finds that she covers an angle of 72° in 1 min. what will be the angle covered by her in 1 second according to the measurement made by her physiotherapist?
o_en: It depends on the position of the coach on the circular track
e_en: Let the athlete runs from A to B in 1 minute and the coach and the physiotherapist observe him from point C and P respectively Given, ∠ACB = 72° The angle subtended by the arc at the centre is double of the angle subtended by the arc at a point on the circle. ⇒ ∠APB = 2 × 72 = 144° Hence, according to physiotherapist the athlete covers an angle of 144° per minute ∴ In 1 second, the angle covered by the athlete according to physiotherapist = 144/60 = 2.4°

q_en: A certain sum was invested on simple interest. The amount to which it had grown in five years was 1 1/4 times the amount to which it had grown in three years. The percentage rate of interest was:
e_en: Let the amount invested be Rs. 100 and the rate of interest be x Simple interest for 5 year = PRT/100 = (100 × x × 5)/100 = 5x ⇒ Amount at the end of 5 years = P + I = 100 + 5x Simple interest for 3 years = PRT/100 = (100 × x × 3)/100 = 3x Amount at the end of 3 years = P + I = 100 + 3x According to question: 100 + 5x = 5/4(100 + 3x) ⇒ 400 + 20x = 500 + 15x ⇒ 5x = 100 ⇒ x = 20%

e_en: By hit and trial method: Taking the value of θ = 90° L.H.S. √3 cosθ + sinθ = √3 cos90° + sin90° = √3 (0) + 1 = 1 = R.H.S. ∴ θ = 90°

q_en: The average of 1088 real numbers is zero. At most how many of them can be negative?
e_en: We know, Average of quantities = sum of all quantities/no. of quantities The average of 1088 numbers is zero. So, the summation of 1088 numbers = 1088 × 0 = 0 If the summation of 1087 numbers = - (1088th number) then only summation of 1088 number will be zero. ∴ Out of 1088 numbers, at most 1087 numbers may be greater than zero.

q_en: A can complete a piece of work in 20 days and B can complete 20% of the work in 6 days. If they work together in how many days can they finish 50% of the work, if they work together?
e_en: A completes a piece of work in 20 days. ⇒ One day work of A = 1/20 B completes 20% of the work in 6 days. ⇒ B will complete 100% of the work in 6 × 100/20 = 30 days. One day work of B = 1/30 When A and B work together, their one day work = 1/20 + 1/30 ⇒ (3 + 2)/60 ⇒ 5/60 ⇒ 1/12 ⇒ A and B working together can complete the whole work in 12 days. ∴ A and B together can complete 50% of the work in 12/2 = 6 days

q_en: A purchased two articles for Rs. 200 and Rs. 300 respectively and sold at gains of 5% and 10% respectively. What was his overall gain percentage?
e_en: Selling price of first article = 200 × 105/100 = Rs. 210 Selling price of second article = 300 × 110/100 = Rs. 330 Total selling price = 210 + 330 = Rs. 540 Total cost price = 200 + 300 = Rs. 500 ∴ Overall gain percentage = (540 – 500)/500 × 100 = 8%

q_en: The distance between the centers of two circles of radius 3 cm and 2 cm is 13 cm. The length (in cm) of a transverse common tangent is:
e_en: Calculation: Let the radius of both circles be R and r and the distance between their center is d Now, R = 3 cm, r = 2 cm and d = 13 cm Transverse common tangent (PQ)= √{d² - (R + r)²} ⇒ √{(13)² - (3 + 2)²} = 12 cm ∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.

q_en: AB and CD are two chords of a circle which intersect at a point O inside the circle. It is given that, AB = 10 cm, CO = 1.5 cm and DO = 12.5 cm. What is the ratio between the larger and smaller among AO and BO?
e_en: Let two chords AB and CD intersect inside the circle at the point O: Hence intersecting chords theorem is used which means that the products of the lengths of the line segments on each chord are equal AO × OB = CO × DO ⇒ x(10 – x) = 1.5 × 12.5 ⇒ 10x – x² = 18.75 ⇒ x² – 10x + 18.75 = 0 ⇒ 100x² – 1000x + 1875 = 0 ⇒ 4x² – 40x + 75 = 0 ⇒ 4x² – 30x – 10x + 75 = 0 ⇒ 2x(2x – 15) – 5(2x – 15) = 0 ⇒ (2x – 5)(2x – 15) = 0 ⇒ x = 5/2 or x = 15/2 When x = 5/2, (10 – x) = (10 – 5/2) = 15/2…

q_en: The two diagonals of a rhombus are respectively, 14 cm and 48 cm. The perimeter of the rhombus is equal to:
e_en: In a rhombus, the diagonals bisect each other at right angle Let the diagonal AC = 14 cm and BD = 48 cm ⇒ AO = 14/2 = 7 cm and BO = 48/2 = 24 cm In ΔAOB, AB² = AO² + BO² ⇒ AB² = 7² + 24² ⇒ AB² = 49 + 576 ⇒ AB² = 625 ⇒ AB = 25 cm ∴ Perimeter of the rhombus = 4 × side of rhombus = 4 × 25 = 100 cm

q_en: A earns Rs. 640 per day and works for 8 hours. B earns 360 per day and works for 6 hours. The ratio of per day wages of A to that of B is:

q_en: The platform of a station 400 m long starts exactly where the last span of a bridge 1.2 km long ends. How long will a train 200 m long and travelling at the speed of 72 km/h take to cover the distance between the starting point of the span of the bride and the far end of the platform?
e_en: The distance between the starting point of the span of the bridge and the far end of the platform = 1200 + 400 = 1600 m When the train crosses the bridge and the platform, it covers the distance = length of the bridge and platform + length of the train ⇒ Distance covered by train = 1600 + 200 = 1800 m Speed of the train = 72 km/hr = 72 × 5/18 = 20 m/s Time = Distance / Speed ⇒ Time = 1800/20 = 90 seconds = 1.5 mins

q_en: The average age of fifteen persons is 32 years. If two more persons are added, then the average is increased by 3 years. The new persons have an age difference of 9 years between them. The age (in years) of the elder among the new persons is:
e_en: Calculation: Total age of 15 persons = 15 × 32 = 480 After adding 2 more persons the new average will be = 32 + 3 = 35 Now the total age of 17 persons = 17 × 35 = 595 Age of two new persons = 595 – 480 = 115 The two new people have an age difference of 9 years Let the age of younger is x year and age of older is x + 9 years ∴ x + x + 9 = 115 ⇒ 2x = 115 – 9 = 106 ⇒ x = 53 ∴ The age of elder person = 53 + 9 = 62 years.

q_en: The ratio between the speeds of two trains is 2 : 5. If the first train runs 250 km in 5 h, then the sum of the speeds (in km/ h) of both the trains is:

q_en: A dealer buys an article marked at Rs. 20000 with two successive discounts of 20% and 5%. He spends Rs. 1800 on repairs and sells it for Rs. 20000, what is his profit/loss percent (correct to one decimal place)?

q_en: The vertices A, B, C and D of a quadrilateral ABCD lie on a circle. ∠A is thrice ∠C and ∠D is twice ∠B. What is the difference between the measures of ∠B and ∠C?
e_en: We know that in cyclic quadrilateral the sum of opposite angle is 180° ∠A + ∠C = 180° ⇒ 3 θ + θ = 180° ⇒ 4 θ = 180° ⇒ θ = 45° ∴ ∠C = 45° Again, ∠B + ∠D = 180° ⇒ α + 2α = 180° ⇒ 3 α = 180° ⇒ α = 60° ∴ ∠B = 60° ∴ Difference between ∠B and ∠C = 60° − 45° = 15°

e_en: We know that in rhombus the diagonal intersects at right angle and equally divide diagonal ∴ In right angle ∆BOC BO = sqrt {{{( {20} )}²} - {{( {12} )}²}} = sqrt {400 - 144} = sqrt {256} = 16 cm ∴ BD = BO + OD = 16 + 16 = 32 cm Also AC = 24 cm (given) Area of rhombus = 1/2 × first diagonal × second diagonal = 1/2 × 32 × 24 = 384 cm²

q_en: In a class of 80 students, 60% participate in games and the rest do not. The average weight of the former group is 5% more than that of the latter. If the average weight of all the students is 51.5 kg, then what is the average weight (in kg) of the former group?
e_en: Total weight = Average weight × Total number Total weight of all the students = 80 × 51.5 = 4120 kg We know that 60% of students participated in games ∴ 60% of 80 = 48 students participated in games And number of students did not participate in games = (80 – 48) = 32 Let the weight of 32 students be x Weight of 48 students = x + x × 5% = 1.05x According to the question, 1.05x × 48 + x × 32 = 4120 ⇒ x = 50kg ∴ the weight (in kg) of the former groupstudents = 1.05x × 50 = 52.5…

q_en: Amit travelled from A to B at an average speed of 80 km/h. He travelled the first 75% of the distance in two-third of the time and the rest at a constant speed of x km/h. The value of x is:
e_en: Given: Average speed = 80 km/hr Formula used: Distance = Speed × time Calculation: Let the distance be y km Time is taken by him = y/80 h 75% of the distance = 75% of y = (3/4)y Time is taken by him to complete the distance of y km = (y/80) × (2/3) = y/120 Rest distance = y&

q_en: Two circles of radii 7 cm and 9 cm intersect at the point A and B. If AB = 10 cm and the distance between the centers of the circles is x cm, then the value of x is:
e_en: We know that radius intersects chord perpendicularly and divides chord two equal parts ∴ AC = 5 cm In ∆APC PC = sqrt {{7²} - {5²}} = sqrt {49 - 25} = sqrt {24} = 2sqrt 6 cm In ∆ACQ QC = sqrt {{9²} - {5²}} = sqrt {81 - 25} = sqrt {56} = 2sqrt {14} cm Distance between centers = PQ = 2 √6 + 2 √14 = 2 (√6 + √14) cm

q_en: A man bought 2 articles for Rs. 3050 each. He sold one article at 10% loss and another at 20% profit. The total profit/loss percentage he earned is:
e_en: Since question asked profit or loss in terms of percentage ∴ we can assume CP of each article is Rs. 100 Total CP = 100 + 100 = Rs. 200 SP of first article = 100 × 90/100 = 90 SP of second article = 100 × 120/100 = 120 Total SP = 90 + 120 = Rs. 210 Profit = 210 – 200 = 10 Profit percentage = (10/200) × 100 = 5 %

q_en: PAT is a tangent to a circle at point A on it, and AB is a chord such that ∠BAT = 72°. If C is a point on the circle such that ∠CBA = 58°, then what is the measure of ∠CAB?
e_en: We know that ∠BAT = ∠BCA ----(angle on the same arc i.e. Arc AB) ∴ ∠BCA = ∠BAT = 72° In Δ ABC ∠ABC + ∠BCA + ∠BAC = 180° ⇒ 58° + 72° + ∠BAC = 180° ⇒ ∠BAC = 180° − 130° = 50° ∴ ∠BAC = 50°

q_en: A number is decreased by 30%, then increased by 30%, then further increased by 30%. What is the net increase/decrease percent in the number (correct to the nearest integer)?
e_en: Calculation: 100 × 70/100 × 130/100 × 130/100 = 118.3 Increase = 118.3 – 100 = 18.3 Percentage increase = (18.3/100) × 100 = 18.3 % = 18 % increase (approx.) ∴ The correct answer is 18%

q_en: In a constituency, 40% of the voters are senior citizens. 40% of the senior citizen voters are illiterates and 25% of the non-senior citizen voters are literates. By what percentage is the number of literate senior citizens voters less than that of illiterate non-senior citizen voters?
e_en: Let total voter be 100 Then senior citizens = 40 and non-senior citizens = 60 Number of literates senior citizens = 24 And number of illiterate senior citizens = 16 Also Number of illiterates non-senior citizens = 45 And number of literate non-senior citizens = 15 The number of literate senior citizens voters less than that of illiterate non-senior citizen voters = 45 – 24 = 21 Required percentage = (21/45) × 100 = 46.66%

q_en: ABCD is a cycle quadrilateral such that AB is a diameter of the circle circumscribing it and ∠ADC = 158°. Then ∠BAC is equal to:
e_en: We know that in cyclic quadrilateral the sum of opposite angle = 180° ⇒ ∠ABC + ∠ADC = 180° ⇒ ∠ABC + 158° = 180° ⇒ ∠ABC = 180° − 158° = 22° In ΔABC We know that angle made by diameter is 90° ∴ ∠ACB = 90° Now, ∠BAC + ∠ABC + ∠ACB = 180° ⇒ ∠BAC + 22° + 90° = 180° ∴ ∠BAC = 180° − 112° = 68°

q_en: Three articles are bought at Rs. 200 each. One of them is sold at a loss of 10%. If the other two articles are sold so as to gain 20% on the whole transaction, then what is the gain percent on the two articles?
e_en: Given: CP of 3 articles is Rs.200 each Total gain percentage on whole transaction = 20% Calculation: Total CP of 3 articles = 200 × 3 = 600 So, SP of all three articles = 600 × 120/100 = 720 SP of 1st article = 200 – 200 × 10% = 180 CP of other 2 article = 400 SP of 2 other article = 720 – 180 = 540 Profit on 2 article = 540 – 400 = 140 Profit percentage of 2 article = (140/400) × 100 = 35% ∴ The gain percent on the two articles is 35%

q_en: If x + y + z = 3 and xy + yz + zx = -18, then what is the value of x³ + y³ + z³ – 3xyz = ?
e_en: Given: x + y + z = 3 and xy + yz + zx = -18 Calculation: x + y + z = 3 Squaring both sides x² + y& lt;sup>2 + z² + 2(xy + yz + zx) = 9 ⇒ x² + y² + z² + 2 × (-18) = 9 ⇒ x² + y² + z² = 9 + 36 = 45 Now x³ + y³ + z³ – 3xyz = (x + y + z) (x² + y² + z² – xy – yz – zx) = 3 × [45 – (-18)] = 3 × 63 = 189 ∴ x³ + y³ + z³ – 3xyz = 189

q_en: Sudha decided to donate 12% of her monthly income to an orphanage. On the day of donation, she changed her decision and donated a sum of Rs. 4800 which was equal to 80% of what she had decide earlier. What is 27% of her monthly income?
e_en: Topper's approach∶ Required income = 4800 ÷ (0.12 × 0.8) × 100 × 0.27 = 13500 Detailed solution∶ Let monthly income be E According to question E × 12% × 80% = 4800 ⇒ E × (12/100) × (80/100) = 4800 ⇒ E = 50000 ∴ Monthly income of Sudha = 50000 ∴ 27% of monthly income = 50000 × 27% = 50000 × 27/100 = 13500 rupees

e_en: Concept used: For successive increase or decrease = x + y + xy/100 Calculation: Percentage change in area of rectangle = - 11 + 11 + (-11)(11)/100 = - 1.21% ∴ The correct option is 4.

q_en: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral such that AB is a diameter of the circle circumscribing it and angle ADC = 146°. ∠BAC is equal to:
e_en: Given: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral. AB is a diameter of the circle Calculation: ∠ADC + ∠ABC = 180° [cyclic quadrilateral the sum of opposite angle is 180°] ⇒ 146° + ∠ABC = 180° ⇒ ∠ABC = 180° − 146° = 34° In ∆ABC ∴ ∠ACB = 90° [angle made by diameter = 90°] ∴ ∠BAC = 180° − (90° + 34°) ⇒ 180° − 124° = 56° ∴ The correct answer is 56°.

q_en: A sum invested at 8% p.a. amounts to Rs. 20280 at the end of one year, when the interest is compounded half yearly. What will be simple interest on the same sum for 4 3/5 years at double the earlier rate of interest?
e_en: Given: Annual rate = 8% Since interest compounded half yearly ∴ r = 4% and time = 2 half yearly Calculation: Let the sum be P P (1 + r/100)t = 20280 ⇒ P (1 + 4/100)² = 20280 ⇒ P × 104/100 × 104/100 = 20280 ⇒ P = 18750 Now, P = 18750 Interest = 8 × 2 = 16% Time = 23/5 year Simple interest = (p × r × t)/100 = (18750 × 16 × 23)/(5 × 100) = 13800 rupees

q_en: The parallel sides of a trapezium are 20 cm and 10 cm and its non-parallel sides are equal to each other. If its area is 180 cm², then what is the length (in cm) of each non-parallel side?
e_en: Area of trapezium = 1/2 (sum of length of parallel sides) × height ⇒ 180 = 1/2 (10 + 20) × height ⇒ height = 12 cm In right angle ∆ADE AD = sqrt {{{( {12} )}²} + {{( 5 )}²}} = sqrt {169} = 13cm ∴ Length of each non-parallel side = 13cm

q_en: A can do 40% of a work in 6 days and B can do 30% of the same work in 3 days. They started the work together but B left after 2 days and A continued to work. In how many days was the entire work completed?
e_en: Concept used: Total work = Efficiency × Time Calculation: A can do 40% of a work in 6 days ∴ A can do 100% of the work in 15 days B can do 30% of the same work in 3 days ∴ B can do 100% of the same work in 10 days Total work = LCM of (15 and 10) = 30 Efficiency of A = 30/15 = 2 Efficiency of B = 30/10 = 3 Work done by A and B together in 2 days = 5 × 2 = 10 Remaining work = 30 – 10 = 20 Remaining work done by A = 20/2 = 10 days ∴ Total Number of days = 10 + 2 = 12 days

q_en: A train covers a certain distance in 45 minutes. If its speed is reduced by 5 km/h, it takes 3 minutes more to cover the same distance. The distance (in km) is:
e_en: Calculation: Let the distance be D km Speed = Distance/Time = D/(45/60) = 60D/45 = (4D/3) km/h The speed of train is reduced by 5 km/h ∴ New speed = (4D/3) – 5 = (4D – 15)/3 km/h New time = 45min + 3min = 48min 48/60 × (4D – 15)/3 = D ⇒ 16 (4D – 15) = 60D ⇒ 4 (4D – 15) = 15D ⇒ 16D – 60 = 15D ⇒ D = 60 ∴ The distance = 60 km

q_en: Incomes of A and B are in the ratio 5 : 3 and their expenditures are in the ratio 9 : 5. If income of A is twice the expenditure of B, then what is the ratio of savings of A and B?
e_en: Ratio of income of A and B = 5 : 3 …(1) Ratio of expenditure of A and B = 9 : 5 …(2) Since income of A is twice the expenditure of B ∴ Multiply eqn..(1) by 2 Now Ratio of income of A and B = 10 : 6 Also Ratio of expenditure of A and B = 9 : 5 ∴ Ratio of saving of A and B = 1 : 1

q_en: If sec θ = 8 x and tan θ = 8/x (x ≠ 0), then the value of 16 (x² − 1/x²) is:
e_en: Given: sec θ = 8x; tan θ = 8/x Formula used: sec2θ - tan2 θ = 1 Calculation: ⇒ (8x)2 – (8/x)2 = sec2θ − tan2 θ ⇒ 64x² – 64/x² = sec2θ − tan2 θ ⇒ 64 (x² – 1/x²) = 1 ⇒ 64 (x² – 1/x²) = 1 Dividing both sides by 4 ⇒ 16 (x² – 1/x²) = 1/4 ∴ The correct answer is 1/4.

q_en: A earns Rs. 100 per hour and works for 8 hours per day. B earns Rs. 120 per hour and works for 6 hours per day. The ratio of per day wages of B to that of A is:
e_en: Given: A earns Rs. 100 per hour and works for 8 hours per day. B earns Rs. 120 per hour and works for 6 hours per day. Calculation: B earns per day = 120 × 6 A earns per day = 100 × 8 Required ratio = 120 × 6 : 100 × 8 = 9 : 10 ∴ The correct answer is 9 : 10.

q_en: A shopkeeper marks his goods at 25% above the cost price. He sells three-fourth of the goods at the marked price and the remaining at 40% discount on the marked price. His gain/loss percent is:
e_en: Let shopkeeper has 400 article Also let the cost price of article = 400 rupees ∴ MP = 400 + 400 × 25% = 500 MP of 1 article = 500/400 = 5/4 3/4 of the article = 400 × 3/4 = 300 SP of 300 article = 300 × 5/4 = 375 Remaining article = 100 SP of remaining article = 100 × 5/4 × 60/100 = 75 Total SP of 400 article = 375 + 75 = 450 Profit = 450 – 400 = 50 Profit percentage = (50/400) ×

q_en: If cos x = -√3/2 and π < x < 3π/2, then the value of 4 cot² x – 3 cosec² x is:
e_en: Given: cos x = −√3/2 Calculation: cos x = −√3/2 ∴ x = 210° Now 4 cot² x – 3 cosec² x ⇒ 4 cot² 210° − 3 cosec² 210° ⇒ 4 × 3 – 3 × 4 ⇒ 12 – 12 = 0 ∴ The correct answer is 0.

q_en: If 7(cosec²57° − tan²33°) + 2 sin90° − 4 tan²52° y tan²38° = y/2, then the value of y is:
e_en: Given: 7(cosec255 - tan235)+ 2 × sin 90 - 4 × tan252 (y × tan238) = y/2 Calculation: ⇒ 7(cosec255 - tan235)+ 2 × sin 90 - 4 × tan252 (y × tan238) = y/2 ⇒ 7(cosec255 - cot255)+ 2 × sin 90 - 4 × tan252 (y × tan238) = y/2 ⇒ 7 × 1 + 2 × 1 - 4 tan2 52 × y/tan2 52 = y/2 ⇒ 9 – 4y = y/2 ⇒ 9 = (y/2) + 4y ⇒ 9 = 9y/2 ⇒ y = 2 ∴ The correct answer is 6.

q_en: If x⁴ + x⁻⁴ = 1154, (x > 0) then the value of 2(x – 3)² is:
If 8(a + b)³ + (a - b)³ = (3a + b) (Aa² + Bab + Cb²), then what is the value of (A + B - C)?
e_en: 8(a + b)³ + (a - b)³ = (3a + b) (Aa² + Bab + Cb²) ⇒ [2(a + b)]³ + (a – b)³ = (3a + b) (Aa² + Bab + Cb²) ⇒ (2a + 2b)³ + (a – b)³ = (3a + b) (Aa² + Bab + Cb²) ⇒ (2a + 2b + a – b) [4a² + 4b² + 8ab + a² + b² – 2ab – (2a² – 2b²)] = (3a + b) (Aa² + Bab + Cb²) ⇒ (3a + b) (3a² + 6ab + 7b²) = (3a + b) (Aa² + Bab + Cb²) ⇒ (3a² + 6ab + 7b²) = (Aa² + Bab + Cb²) By comparing both sides A = 3, B = 6 and C = 7 Now, (A + B - C) = (3 + 6 – 7) = 2 ∴ (A + B - C) = 2

q_en: In ΔABC, ∠A = 72°. Its sides AB and AC are produced to the points D and E respectively. If the bisectors of the ∠CBD and ∠BCE meet at point O, then ∠BOC is equal to:
e_en: Given: ∠BAC = 72° Calculation: ⇒ ∠BOC = 90° - ∠A/2 ⇒ ∠BOC = 90° - (72°/2) ⇒ ∠BOC = 90° - 36° ⇒ ∠BOC = 54° ∴ The correct answer is 54°.

q_en: The compound interest on a certain sum of money at 21% for 2 years is Rs. 11,602.5. Its simple interest (in Rs.) at the same rate and for the same period is:
e_en: Given: C.I = Rs. 11,602.5, rate = 21%, time = 2 years Formula used: Compound interest = P [(1 + r/100)n – 1] Where, P = Principal amount, r = Rate of interest, n = Number of years Calculation: Compound interest = P × [(1 + r/100)n – 1] ⇒ 11,602.5 = P × [(1 + 21/100)2 – 1] ⇒ 11,602.5 = P × [1.4641 - 1] ⇒ 11,602.5 = P × 0.4641 ⇒ P = 25000 Now, S.I = (P × R × T)/100 ⇒ (25000 × 21 × 2)/100 ⇒ 10,500 ∴ The correct answer is Rs.10,500.

q_en: If a 10-digit number 75y97405x2 is divisible by 72, then the value of (2x - y), for the greatest value of x, is:
e_en: Concept used: When a number is divisible by 72 then it must be divisible by 8 × 9 When a number is divisible by 8 then its last 3 digit must be divisible by 8 Calculation: 5x2 is divisible by 8 When x = 5 or x = 9 We have to take greatest value of x So x = 9 When a number is divisible by 9 then the sum of its digit must be multiple of 9 7 + 5 + y + 9 + 7 + 4 + 0 + 5 + 9 + 2 = 48 + y So the possible value of y = 6 ∴ 2x – y = 2 × 9 – 6 = 12

q_en: The distance between the centers of two circles of a radius of 6 cm each is 13 cm. The length (in cm) of a transverse common tangent is:
e_en: Given: Distance between center(d) = 13 cm r1 = 6 cm and r2 = 6 cm Formula used: Length of transverse common tangent = √{d² - (r₁ + r₂)²} Calculation: Length of transverse common tangent = √{d2 - (r1 + r2)2} Length of transverse tangent = √{(13)2 - (6 + 6)2} ⇒ √{169 - 144} = √25 = 5 cm ∴ The correct answer is 5 cm.

q_en: A dealer buys an article marked at Rs. 5000 with two successive discounts of 20% and 5%. He spends Rs. 200 on repairs and sells it for Rs. 5000, what is his profit/loss percent?
e_en: Calculation: CP for dealer = 5000 × (80/100) × (95/100) = Rs. 3800 After spending Rs. 200 on repairs Total CP for dealer = 3800 + 200 = Rs. 4000 SP of dealer = Rs. 5000 Profit = 5000 – 4000 = Rs. 1000 Profit percentage = (1000/4000) × 100 = 25% ∴ The correct answer is 25%.

q_en: The sum of the salaries of A and B is Rs. 42,000. A spends 75% of his salary and B spends 90% of his salary. Now their savings are the same. What is A’s salary (in Rs.)?
e_en: Given: The sum of the salaries of A and B is Rs. 42,000. A spends 75% of his salary and B spends 90% of his salary. Their savings are the equal. Calculation: Since their savings are same ∴ A × 25% = B × 10% ⇒ 5 A = 2 B ⇒ A/B = 2/5 Let the salaries of A and B be 2x and 5x respectively ∴ 2x + 5x = 42,000 ⇒ 7x = 42,000 ⇒ x = 6,000 Salary of A = 2 × 6000 = Rs. 12000 ∴ The correct answer is Rs. 12000.

q_en: A and B can complete a piece of work in 15 days and 20 days respectively. They got a contract to complete the work Rs. 77000. The share of A (in Rs) in the contracted money will be:
e_en: Given: A can complete a piece of work = 15 days B can complete a piece of work = 20 days Total money = Rs. 77000 Concept used: When the work is equal Time ∝ 1/Efficiency Calculation: Ratio of number of days taken by A and B to complete the work ⇒ 15 : 20 = 3 : 4 Ration of efficiency of A and B = 4 : 3 Let share of A in money be 4x and B in money be 3x ⇒ 4x + 3x = 77000 ⇒ 7x = 77000 ⇒ x = Rs. 11000 A = 4x = 4 × 11000 = Rs. 44000 ∴ Share of A in money = Rs. 44000

q_en: A circle is inscribed in a triangle ABC. It touches sides AB, BC and AC at points P, Q and R respectively. If BP = 9 cm, CQ = 10 cm and AR = 11 cm, then the perimeter (in cm) of the triangle ∆ABC is
e_en: Two tangents drawn from external point on the circle are equal ∴ AP = AR = 11 cm BP = BQ = 9 cm And CQ = CR = 10cm ∴ Perimeter of triangle = 11 + 11 + 9 + 9 + 10 + 10 = 60 cm

q_en: If 2 sin²θ + 5 cos θ – 4 = 0, 0° < θ < 90°, then the value of cot θ + cosec θ is:
e_en: Given: 2 sin²θ + 5 cos θ – 4 = 0 Concept used: sin2θ = (1 – cos2θ) Calculation: 2 sin2θ + 5 cos θ – 4 = 0 ⇒ 2 (1 – cos²θ) + 5 cos θ – 4 = 0 ⇒ 2 – 2 cos² θ + 5 cos θ – 4 = 0 ⇒ 2 cos²θ – 5 cos θ + 2 = 0 ⇒ 2 cos²θ – 4 cos θ – cos θ + 2 = 0 ⇒ 2 cos θ (cos θ – 2) – 1 (cos θ – 2) = 0 ⇒ (2 cos θ – 1) (cos θ – 2) = 0 ⇒ cos θ = 1/2 or cos θ = 2 (not possible) ∴ cos θ = 1/2 = cos 60° ∴ θ = 60° Now cot θ + cosec θ = cot 60° + cosec 60° = (1/√3) + (2/√3) = 3/√3 = √3 ∴ cot θ + cosec θ = √…

q_en: Three number are in the ratio 1/2 : 2/3 : 3/4. The difference between the greatest and the smallest number is 27. The average of the three number is:
e_en: The given ratio of three numbers 1/2 : 2/3 : 3/4 ⇒ 6 : 8 : 9 Let the numbers be 6x, 8x and 9x According to question Difference between the greatest and the smallest number = 27 ⇒ 9x – 6x = 27 ⇒ 3x = 27 ⇒ x = 9 The first number = 6x = 6 × 9 = 54 The Second number = 8x = 8 × 9 = 72 The third number = 9x = 9 × 9 = 81 Sum of three numbers = 54 + 72 + 81 = 207 ∴ Average = 207/3 = 69

q_en: Let ΔABC ~ ΔQPR and ar(∆ABC)/ar(∆PQR) = 4/25. If AB = 12 cm, BC = 8 cm and AC = 10 cm, then QP is equal to:
e_en: Given: ΔABC ~ ΔQPR Ar (∆ABC)/Ar (∆PQR) = 4/25 Calculation: ∵ ΔABC ∼ Δ QPR ⇒ (AB/PQ)² = Ar(∆ABC)/Ar(∆PQR) ⇒ (12/PQ)² = 4/25 ⇒ 12/PQ = 2/5 ⇒ PQ = 30 cm ∴ The correct answer is 30 cm.

q_en: A man bought three articles for Rs. 6,000 each. He sold the article respectively at 15% profit, 12% profit and 15% loss. The total percentage profit/loss he earned is:
e_en: Given: A man bought three articles for Rs. 6,000 each. Calculation: Let the CP of each article = 100. Total CP of 3 articles = 300 SP of first article = 100 × 115/100 = 115 SP of second article = 100 × 112/100 = 112 SP of third article = 100 × 85/100 = 85 Total CP of 3 articles = 115 + 112 + 85 = Rs. 312 Profit = 312 – 300 = Rs. 12 Profit Percentage = (12/300) × 100 = 4% ∴ The correct answer is 4%.

q_en: 9 years ago, the average age of a family of five members was 33 years. Now, three new members join whose ages are in ascending order with consecutive gaps of 8 years. If the present average age of the family is the same as it was 9 years ago, what is the age (in years) of the eldest new member?
e_en: 9 years ago, The total age of 5 members = 33 × 5 = 165 Now total age of 8 members = 33 × 8 = 264 And total age of 5 members = 165 + 45 = 210 Total age of 3 new members = 264 – 210 = 54 Now let the age of new younger member = x ∴ age of middle member = x + 8 And age of eldest member = x + 16 According to question x + x + 8 + x + 16 = 54 ⇒ 3x + 24 = 54 ⇒ 3x = 30 ⇒ x = 10 ∴ The age of eldest person = x + 16 = 10 + 16 = 26 year

q_en: If 12 cot²θ – 31 cosec θ + 32 = 0, 0° < θ < 90°, then the values of sin θ will be:
e_en: 12 cot²θ – 31 cosec θ + 32 = 0 ⇒ 12(cosec²θ – 1) – 31 cosec θ + 32 = 0 ⇒ 12 cosec²θ – 12 – 31 cosec θ + 32 = 0 ⇒ 12 cosec²θ – 31 cosec θ + 20 = 0 ⇒ 12 cosec²θ – 16 cosec θ – 15 cosec θ + 20 = 0 ⇒ 4 cosec θ (3 cosec θ – 4) – 5 (3 cosec θ – 4) = 0 ⇒ (4 cosec θ – 5) (3 cosec θ – 4) = 0 ⇒ cosec θ = 5/4 or cosec θ = 4/3 ∴ sin θ = 4/5 or sin θ = 3/4

q_en: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral such that its sides AD and BC produced meet at P and sides AB and DC produced meet at O. If ∠A = 62° and ∠ABC = 74°, then the difference between ∠P and ∠O is:

q_en: The average of n numbers is 36. If each of 75% of the numbers is increased by 6 and each of the remaining numbers is decreased by 9, then the new average of the numbers is:
e_en: Let the total number = 100 Average = 36 (given) Total = 36 × 100 = 3600 75% of 100 = 75 Total increase in 75 numbers = 75 × 6 = 450 Total decrease in 25 numbers = 25 × -9 = 225 ∴ Total increase in 100 numbers = 450 – 225 = 225 Now Total = 3600 + 225 = 3825 Average = 3825/100 = 38.25%

q_en: If (2x - 7)³ + (2x – 8)³ + (2x - 3)³ = 3 (2x - 7) (2x - 8) (2x - 3), then what is the value of x?

q_en: Two students, A and B, appeared for an examination. A secured 8 marks more than B and the marks of the former was 55% of the sum of their marks. The marks obtained by A and B, respectively, are:

q_en: Two numbers are in the ratio of 7 : 5. On diminishing each of them by 40, the ratio becomes 27 : 17. The sum of the numbers is:

q_en: If a³ – b³ = 899 and a – b = 31, then (a – b)² + 3ab is equal to:
e_en: Given: ⇒ a3 - b3 = 899 ⇒ a - b = 31 Formula used: (a - b)² = a² + b² - 2ab a3 - b3 = (a - b) (a2 + b2 + ab) Calculation: ⇒ a³ - b³ = (a - b) × (a² + b² + ab) ⇒ a³ - b³ = (a - b) × (a² + b² + ab + 2ab - 2ab) ⇒ a³ - b³ = (a - b) × ((a² + b² - 2ab) + 3ab) ⇒ a³ - b³ = (a - b) × ((a - b)² + 3ab) Putting the values, ⇒ (a³ - b³) / (a - b) = (a - b)² + 3ab ⇒ 899/31 = (a - b)² + 3ab ⇒ (a - b)² + 3ab = 29 ∴ The correct answer is 29.

q_en: A dealer buys an article marked at Rs. 30000 with two successive discounts of 20% and 5%. He spends Rs. 1200 on repairs and sells it for Rs. 30000, what is his profit/loss percent?
e_en: Calculation: C.P of article = marked price × 80% × 95% So, C.P of article = 30000 × 4/5 × 19/20 = 22800 Additional expenditure = 1200 So, total C.P of article = 22800 + 1200 = 24000 Given that S.P of article = 30000 So, gain = 30000 – 24000 = 6000 Gain% = (gain /C.P) × 100 Gain% = (6000/24000) × 100 = 25% ∴ The correct answer is 25%.

e_en: Given: The sum of the salaries of A and B is Rs. 42,000. Calculation: A spends 75% of his salary, his saving 25% of his salary B spends 90% of his salary, his saving 10% of his salary According to condition, Saving of A = saving of B ⇒ 25% A = 10% B ⇒ A : B = 2 : 5 Now salary of B = (5/7) × 42,000 = 5 × 6, 000 = 30,000 ∴ The correct answer is Rs.30000.

q_en: If the seven digit number 64x29y6 (x > y) is divisible by 72, what is the value of (2x – 3y)?
e_en: Calculation: ⇒ 72 = 9 × 8, where 9 and 8 are co–prime ⇒ 64x29y6 is should be divisible by 9 and 8 Divisibility rule of 8, ⇒ Last three digits 9y6 so minimum value of y = 3 Divisibility rule of 9, ⇒ 30 + x also divisible by 9 so x = 6 The value of (2x – 3y) = 12 – 9 = 3 ∴ The correct answer is 3.

q_en: If x + y + z = 10, x³ + y³ + z³ = 75 and xyz = 15, then find the value of x² + y² + z² – xy – yz – zx
e_en: Given: x + y + z = 10, (x³ + y³ + z³) = 75 and xyz = 15 Formula: (x³ + y³ + z³ - 3xyz) = (x + y + z) (x² + y² + z² - xy - yz - zx) Calculation: According to the given formula (x3 + y3 + z3 - 3xyz) = (x + y + z) (x2 + y2 + z2 - xy - yz - zx) ⇒ 75 - 3 × 15 = 10 × (x2 + y2 + z2 - xy - yz - zx) ⇒ 75 - 45 = 10 × (x2 + y2 + z2 - xy - yz - zx) ⇒ (x2 + y2 + z2 - xy - yz - zx) = 30/10 ∴ x2 + y2 + z2 - xy - yz - zx = 3

q_en: Length and breadth of rectangular field are in the ratio 5 ∶ 2. If the perimeter of the field is 238 m. Find the length of the field.
e_en: Given: Ratio of length and breadth of the rectangular field = 5 : 2. Perimeter of the rectangular field = 238 m. Formula: Perimeter of the rectangle = 2(l + b) Calculation: Ratio of length and breadth of the rectangular field = 5x : 2x According to the question 2 × (5x + 2x) = 238 ⇒ 2 × 7x = 238 ⇒ x = 238/14 ⇒ x = 17 m ∴ Length of the field = 5 × 17 = 85 m.

q_en: Mohan offers to sell his articles at a discount of 20%, but he marks his articles by increasing the price of each by 35%. What percentage would his gain be?
e_en: Given: Discount = 20% MP is more than CP by 35% Formula: Profit = SP – CP Profit % = (Profit/CP) × 100 Calculation: Let CP of the articles be Rs. 100 MP of the articles = 100 × (135/100) = Rs. 135 Now, SP of the articles = 135 × (80/100) = Rs. 108 Profit = Rs. 108 - Rs. 100 = Rs. 8 ∴ Profit percentage = (8/100) × 100 = 8%

q_en: 30 men working 8 hours per day can dig a pond in 16 days. By working how many hours per day can 32 men dig the same pond in 20 days?
e_en: Given: 30 men working 8 hours per day can dig a pond in = 16 days Formula: M₁ × T₁ × D₁ = M₂ × T₂ × D₂ Calculation: M₁ = 30 men, T₁ = 8 hrs, D₁ = 16 days, M₂ = 32 men, D₂ = 20 days According to the formula 30 × 8 × 16 = 32 × T₂ × 20 ⇒ T₂ = (30 × 8 × 16)/(32 × 20) ∴ T₂ = 6 hrs.

q_en: Rs. 3,600 is divided between Seema, Komal and Rita, such that the ratios of the shares of Seema ∶ Komal = 1.5 ∶ 2 and Komal ∶ Rita = 2 ∶ 2.5. Find Rita's share.
e_en: Given: Total amount to be divided among Seema, Komal and Rita = Rs. 3600 Ratio of shares of Seema and Komal = 1.5 : 2 Ratio of shares of Komal and Rita = 2 : 2.5 Calculation: Ratio of shares of Seema and Komal = 1.5x : 2 x Ratio of shares of Komal and Rita = 2x : 2.5x Ratio of shares of Seema, Komal and Rita = 1.5x : 2x : 2.5x According to the question 1.5x + 2x + 2.5x = 3600 ⇒ 6x = 3600 ⇒ x = 3600/6 ⇒ x = 600 ∴ Share of Rita = 2.5 × 600 = Rs. 1,500

q_en: PQR is an isosceles triangle such that PQ = QR = 10 cm and ∠ PQR = 90°. What is the length of the perpendicular drawn from Q on PR?
e_en: Given: PQ = QR = 10 cm ∠PQR = 90° Formula: Area of triangle = (1/2) × Base × Height (Hypotenuse)² = (Base)² + (Perpendicular)² Calculation: PR² = 10² + 10² ⇒ PR² = 100 + 100 ⇒ PR² = 200 ⇒ PR = 10√2 Let QM is perpendicular to PR, then (1/2) × 10 × 10 = (1/2) × QM × 10√2 [Formula of area] ∴ QM = 5√2 cm.

q_en: A runner is running at a speed of 40 km/h. If he runs at a speed of 30 km/h, then what will the decrease in the percentage of his speed be?
e_en: Given: A runner is running at a speed = 40 km/hr Calculation: His speed in starting = 40 km/hr His speed in last = 30 km/hr He decreases his speed = 40 - 30 = 10 km/hr ∴ He decreases his speed (in %) = (10/40) × 100 = 25%

q_en: The average of the runs of a cricket player in 20 matches is 35. If the average of the first 12 matches is 45, find the average of the last 8 matches.
e_en: Given: Average runs of player in 20 matches = 35 Average runs of player in first 12 matches = 45 Formula: Average = (Sum of all observations)/(Total number of all observations) Calculation: Sum of runs of player in 20 matches = 35 × 20 = 700 Sum of runs of player in first 12 matches = 12 × 45 = 540 Sum of runs of player in last 8 matches = 700 - 540 = 160 ∴ Average runs of player in last 8 matches = 160/8 = 20

q_en: Ram sold a motorcycle for Rs. 70000 at 25% profit. For what price should he sell a motorcycle to gain 30% profit?

q_en: The average age of 25 men is 28 years. 5 new men of an average age of 25 years joined them. Find the average age of all the men together.
e_en: Given: Average age of 25 men = 28 years Formula Used: Average = Sum of all observations/Total number of all observations Calculation: Sum of age of 25 men = 28 × 25 = 700 If 5 men of average age of 25 years joined them, Sum of age of 5 men = 25 × 5 = 125 years Now, Sum of age of 30 men = 700 + 125 = 825 years ⇒ Average age of 30 men = 825/30 = 27.5 years ∴ The average age of all the men together is 27.5 years.

q_en: If a + b + c =2,(1)/(a) + (1)/(b)+frac {1}{c}=0, ac=(4)/(b) and a³ + b³ + c³ = 28, find the value of a² + b² + c²
e_en: Given: a + b + c = 2, 1/a + 1/b + 1/c = 0, ac = 4/b and a³ + b³ + c³ = 28 Formula: a³ + b³ + c³ - 3abc = (a + b + c) (a² + b² + c² - ab - bc - ca) Calculation: 1/a + 1/b + 1/c = 0 ⇒ (ab + bc + ca)/abc = 0 ⇒ ab + bc + ca = 0 Also, ac = 4/b ⇒ abc = 4 According to the question a3 + b3 + c3 - 3abc = (a + b + c) (a2 + b2 + c2 - ab - bc - ca) ⇒ 28 - 3 × 4 = 2 × (a² + b² + c² - 0) ⇒ (28 - 12)/2 = a2 + b2 + c2 ⇒ a2 + b2 + c² = 16/2 ⇒ a2 + b2 + c² = 8 ∴ The value of a2 + b2 + c2 is 8.

q_en: Rs. 6,300 is divided between X, Y, Z, such that X : Y = 7 : 5 and Y : Z = 4 : 3. Find the share of Y.
e_en: Given: Total amount which is divided among A, B and C = Rs. 6,300 X : Y = 7 : 5 and Y : Z = 4 : 3 Calculation: X : Y = 7 : 5 ----(1) Y : Z = 4 : 3 ----(2) Multiply by 4 in equation (1) and multiply by 5 in equation (2) X : Y : Z = 28 : 20 : 15 Ratio of X : Y : Z = 28x : 20x : 15x According to the question 28x + 20x + 15x = 6,300 ⇒ 63x = 6,300 ⇒ x = 6,300/63 ⇒ x = 100 ∴ Share of Y = 20 × 100 = Rs. 2,000

Formula: Dividend = Divisor × Quotient + Remainder Calculation: Let quotient be q, then n = 5q + 3 Multiply by 8 in equation (1) ⇒ 8n = 40q + 24 ⇒ 8n = 40q + 20 + 4 ⇒ 8n = 5 × (8q + 4) + 4 ∴ Now we can say remainder is 4. Let n be 8. [Satisfied the given condition] Now, 8n = 8 × 8 = 64 When we divide 64 by 5, we will have 4 as the remainder.

q_en: The perimeter and length of a rectangle are in the ratio of 8 : 1, and the area of the rectangle is 1323 cm². Find the length of the rectangle.

q_en: The value of a motorcycle depreciates every year by 4%. What will be its value after 2 years, if its present value is Rs. 75,000?
e_en: Solution: Given data: Present value of motorcycle = Rs. 75,000 Rate of depreciation = 4% Time for depreciation = 2 years Concept used: Final value = Initial value × [(100 – Rate of depreciation)/100]ⁿ Where, n = no. of years Calculation: Final value = Initial value × [(100 – Rate of depreciation)/100]ⁿ ⇒ 75,000 × [(100 – 4)/100]² ⇒ 75,000 × (96/100)² ⇒ 75,000 × (24/25)² ⇒ (75,000 × 576)/625 ⇒ 69,120 ∴ The value of the motorcycle after 2 years will be Rs. 69,120.

q_en: Salma buys an article and then sells if for Rs. 810. If she loses 10%, then at what price should she sell it to gain 4%?

q_en: What number must be added to each of the numbers 8, 13, 26 and 40 so that the numbers obtained in this order are in proportion?

q_en: A player has a certain average for 15 innings. In the 16th inning, he scores 120, thereby his average increased by 6 runs. What is the new average?

q_en: A man took a loan from a bank at the rate of 11% p.a. simple interest. After three years, he had to pay Rs. 9570 interest only for the period. The principal amount borrowed by him was:

q_en: Amit sold an article for Rs. 7,000 and incurred a loss. Had he sold it for Rs. 8,750, his gain would have been three-fourth of the amount of loss that he incurred. At what price should he sell the article to get 10% profit?
e_en: Given: S.P = Rs. 7000 Formula: Profit = S.P – C.P Loss = C.P – S.P Calculation: Let loss be x C.P = S.P + x ⇒ C.P =7000 + x Now, S.P = 8750 Rs Gain = (3/4) × Loss ⇒ S.P – C.P = x × 3/4 ⇒ 8750 - (7000 + x) = 3x/4 ⇒ 8750 – 7000 – x = 3x/4 ⇒ 1750 = 3x/4 + x ⇒ x = 1000 Rs C.P = 7000 + x = 7000 + 1000 ⇒ C.P = 8000 Rs For 10% profit S.P = (8000 × 110)/100 ⇒ S.P = 8800 Rs ∴ S.P to gain 10% profit is 8800 Rs

q_en: If {x⁴} + (1)/({{x⁴)}} = 14159, then the value of x + (1)/(x) is:
e_en: Given: {x⁴} + (1)/({{x⁴)}} = 14159 Formula used: (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab Calculation: x⁴ + 1/x⁴ = 14159 Adding 2 on both sides, ⇒ x⁴ + 1/x⁴ + 2 = 14159 + 2 ⇒ (x² + 1/x²)² = 14161 Taking square root both sides ⇒ (x² + 1/x²) = √(14161) ⇒ (x² + 1/x²) = 119 Adding 2 on both sides, ⇒ x² + 1/x² + 2 = 119 + 2 ⇒ (x + 1/x)² = 121 Taking square root both sides ⇒ x + 1/x = √121 ⇒ x + 1/x = 11 ∴ The value of x + 1/x is 11.

q_en: If a³ + b³ = 20 and a + b = 5, then find the value of a⁴ + b⁴

q_en: If x³ + y³ = 16 and x + y = 4, then the value of x⁴ + y⁴ is:

q_en: ABC and BDE are two equilateral triangles such that D is the mid-point of BC. If the area of triangle ABC is 136 cm², then the area of triangle BDE is equal to:

Calculation: If each side of ΔABC = 2x unit Then, Area of ΔABC = √3 x² ---- (1) Now, BD = BC/2 ( given) ⇒ BD = 2x/2 = x So, area of equilateral triangle BDE =√3x²/4 ---- (2) ⇒ By dividing (1) by (2) ⇒ ar(ΔABC)/ar(ΔBDE) = (√3x²)/(√3x²/4) = 4/1 ⇒ 4 : 1 ⇒ Area of ΔABC = 136 ⇒ 4x = 136 ⇒ x = 34 ∴ The area of ΔBDE is 34 cm²

e_en: Given: √3cosθ = sinθ calculation: ⇒ sinθ/cosθ = √3 ⇒ tanθ = √3 ⇒ θ = 60° Then, (4sin² θ - 5 cos θ)/(3 cos θ + 1) = [4(√3/2)² - (5/2)]/[(3/2) + 1] ⇒ (1/2)/(5/2) = 1/5 ∴ The required value is 1/5.

q_en: An article was sold at a loss of 12%. If it was sold for Rs. 630 more, then there would have been a gain of 6%. Find the cost price of the article.
e_en: Formula used: Cost price = (selling price)/(100 + profit%) × 100 Calculation: Let the cost price of article 100x Sell at 12% loss = 88x Sell at 6% gain = 106x 106x - 88x = 630 ⇒ x = 630/18 = 35 ⇒ 100x = 100 × 35 = 3500 ∴ The cost price of article is Rs 3500

q_en: If the difference between the compound interest and simple interest on a certain sum of money for three years at 10% p.a. is Rs. 558, then the sum is:
e_en: Given: The difference in compound interest and simple interest for 3 years = Rs 558 Rate of interest = 10% Formula Used: Simple interest = principal × rate × time/100 Compound interest = p[(1 + r/100)t - 1] Calculation: Let the principal be p 558 = p[(1 + 10/100)³ - 1] - 3p/10 ⇒ 558 = p[331/1000 - 3/10] ⇒ p = 558 × (1000/31) = 18000 ∴ The sum is Rs 18000

q_en: The salaries of Vipin and Dinesh are in the ratio 5 : 8. If the salary of each is increased by Rs. 4,800. then new ratio becomes 7 : 10. What is Vipin’s salary ?
e_en: Given: The salary of each increased = Rs 4800 Calculation: let the salary of vipin and Dinesh be 5x and 8x (5x + 4800)/(8x + 4800) = 7/10 ⇒ 50x + 48000 = 56x + 33600 ⇒ x = 14400/6 = 2400 Vipin salary = 5x = 5 × 2400 = Rs 12000 ∴ Vipin's salary is Rs 12000

q_en: The perimeter of a rectangular field is 32 metres and its sides are in the ratio 5 : 3. Then the sides of the field are:
e_en: Given: The perimeter of rectangular field = 32 m Formula Used: Perimeter of rectangle = 2(length + breadth) Calculation: ⇒ let the length and breadth be 5a and 3a respectively ⇒ 32 = 2(5a + 3a) ⇒ 16 = 8a ⇒ a = 2 ⇒ so, length = 5 × 2 = 10 m, breadth = 3 × 2 = 6 m ∴ the length and breadth of rectangle is 10 m and 6 m respectively

q_en: The average of nine 2 digit numbers is decreased by 6 when the digits of one of the 2 digit numbers is interchanged. Find the difference between the digits of that number.
e_en: Given: The average of nine 2 digit number decreases by = 6 Formula Used: Average = Sum of Observation/ No. of Observation Calculation: Let the number be 10x+y (Sum of eight numbers + 10x + y)/9 - 6 = (Sum of eight numbers + 10y + x)/9 ⇒ (Sum of eight numbers + 10x + y) - 54 = (Sum of eight numbers + 10y + x) ⇒ 10x + y - 54 = 10y + x ⇒ 9x - 9y = 54 ⇒ x - y = 6 ∴ The difference between the digit of number is 6.

q_en: The difference of two positive numbers is 1020. If 7.6% of the greater number is 12.4% of the smaller number, then the sum of the two numbers is equal to:
e_en: Given: the difference of 2 positive number = 1020 Calculation: ⇒ Let two numbers be x and y resp. ⇒ 7.6% of x = 12.4% of y ⇒ x : y = 31 : 19 ⇒ x - y = 1020 ⇒ 31a - 19a = 1020 ⇒ a = 1020/12 = 85 ⇒ sum of two numbers = 31a + 19a = 50a ⇒ 50 × 85 = 4250 ∴ The sum of two numbers is 4250

q_en: ABC is a right angled triangle, right angled at A. A circle is inscribed in it. The lengths of two sides containing the right angle are 48 cm and 14 cm. The radius of the inscribed circle is:
e_en: Given: AB = 48 cm AC = 14 cm Figure: Formula used: (Hypotnuese)² = Perpendicular²+ base² Area of triangle = 1/2 × Base × Height Calculation: Let OP = OQ = OR = radius = r cm BC² = AB² +AC² ⇒ BC = √(48² + 14²) = 50 cm Area of Δ ABC = area of Δ OAB + area of Δ OBC + area of Δ OAC ⇒ 1/2 × 48 × 14 = 1/2 × [48r + 14r + 50r] ⇒ r = 48 × 14/(112) = 6 cm ∴ The radius of incircle is 6 cm

q_en: Anu purchased a car and then sold it. If the ratio of the cost price and selling price is 10 : 11, then the profit percentage is:
e_en: Given: Ratio of cost price and selling price = 10 : 11 Formula Used: Profit% = (profit/cp) × 100 Profit = sp - cp Calculation: ⇒ let the cost price and selling price be 10x ad 11x ⇒ Profit = 11x - 10x = x ⇒ Profit % = (x/10x) × 100 = 10% ∴ the profit percentage is 10%

q_en: If 3.96 cubic dm of lead is to be drawn in to a cylindrical wire of diameter 0.6 cm, then the length of the wire (in metres), is:
e_en: Given: Diameter of cylindrical wire = .6cm Formula Used: Volume of cylinder = πR²H Calculation: 1 dm = 10 cm 1 dm³ = 1000 cm³ So, 3.96 dm³ = 3960 cm³ Volume of the cylinder = πR²l 3960 = (22/7) × (.6/2)² × l ⇒ l = 14000 cm ⇒ 1m = 100cm ⇒14000 cm = 140 m ∴ The length of cylindrical wire is 140 m

q_en: Ravi and Mohan together can complete a task in 3 days. Ravi alone can complete the same task in 7 days. How many days will Mohan alone take to complete the same task?
e_en: Given: Ravi and Mohan can complete work = 3 days Ravi alone complete the work = 7 days Formula Used: Work = time × efficiency Calculation: ⇒ LCM of (3, 7) = 21 ⇒ Let the total work be 21 ⇒ Efficiency of Ravi and Mohan together = 21/3 = 7 ⇒ Efficiency of Ravi alone = 21/7 = 3 ⇒ Efficiency of Mohan = 7 - 3 = 4 ⇒ Mohan takes time to complete the work alone = 21/4 = 5 1/4 days

q_en: The income of Renu is 10% less than the income of Sudha, and the income of Sudha is 10% more than Rs. 3,000. The income of Renu is:
e_en: Given: The income of renu = 90% of sudha Calculation: ⇒ Income of Sudha = 3000 + 10% of 3000 = Rs 3300 ⇒ Income of Renu = 90% of 3300 = (90/100) × 3300 ⇒ 2970 ∴ the income of Renu is Rs 2970

q_en: The difference between the compound interest and the simple interest on a sum of Rs. 8,000 for 2 years at the rate of 5% p.a. is:
e_en: Given: Principal = Rs 8000 Time = 2 years Rate of interest = 5% Formula Used: Simple interest = Principal × rate × time/100 Compound interest = principal[(1 + r/100)t - 1) Calculation: ⇒ simple interest = (8000 × 2 × 5)/100 = Rs 800 ⇒ compound interest = 8000[(1 + 1/20)² - 1] = 8000 × 41/400 = Rs 820 ⇒ the difference between simple interest and compound interest = Rs 820 - Rs 800 = Rs 20

q_en: If xsin³θ + ycos³θ = sinθ cosθ and xsinθ = ycosθ, then the value of x² + y² is:
e_en: Given: xsin3θ + ycos3θ = sinθ cosθ xsinθ = ycosθ Formula used: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 Calculation: x sin³ θ + y cos³ θ = sin θ cos θ ⇒ (x sin θ) sin² θ + (y cos θ) cos² θ = sin θ cos θ ⇒ (x sin θ) sin² θ + (x sin θ) cos² θ = sin θ cos θ ( y cos θ = x sin θ) ⇒ x sin θ(sin² θ + cos² θ) = sin θ cos θ ⇒ x sin θ = sin θ cos θ ⇒ x = cos θ ----(1) Again x sin θ = y cos θ ⇒ cos θ sin θ = y cos θ ⇒ y = sin θ ----(2) from (1) and (2) ⇒ x² + y² = sin2θ + cos2θ = 1

q_en: The marked price of a book is Rs. 540. After 10% discount on the marked price, the selling price of the book is:
e_en: Given: Marked price of a books = Rs 540 Formula Used: Discount = Marked price - selling price Discount % =(discount/marked) × 100 Calculation: ⇒ 10% = (Discount/540) × 100 ⇒ Discount = 54 ⇒ Selling price = Marked price - discount ⇒ SP = 540 - 54 = Rs 486 ∴ The selling price of books is Rs 486

q_en: In a circle centered at O, AB is a chord and C is any point on AB such that OC is perpendicular to AB. If the radius of the circle is 10 cm and OC = 6 cm, then the length of the chord is:
e_en: Given: Radius of circle = 10 cm distance b/w center and chord = 6 cm Formula Used: (Hypotnuese)² = (Perpendicular)² + (Base)² Calculation: ⇒ radius of circle = hypotuese = 10 cm ⇒ distance b/w center and chord = perpendicular = 6cm ⇒ so, length of chord = 2 × Base ⇒ 10² = 6² + Base² ⇒ Base = 8 cm ⇒ so, length of chord = 2 × 8 = 16 cm ∴ the length of chord AB is 16 cm

q_en: Abhi finishes a journey by car in 9 hours. He travels the first half of the journey at a speed 40 km/h and the second half of the journey at a speed of 50 km/h. The total distance covered is:
e_en: Given: Abhi takes time = 9 hrs Formula Used: Time = Distance/speed Calculation: Let the distance be covered by Abhi be 2x ⇒ 9 hrs = (x/40) + (x/50) ⇒ x = (9 × 2000)/90 ⇒ x = 200 km ∴ the total distance covered by Abhi = 2x = 400 km

q_en: If the number 62783 xy is divisible by both 8 and 5, then the smallest possible value of x and y is:
e_en: Given: Number = 62783xy Concept Used: if no. is divisible by 8, then last 3 digit of that number should be divisible by 8 if any no. is divisible by 5, then unit digit comes 0 or 5 Calculation: ⇒ we know that the value of y = 0, 5 ⇒ if we consider y = 5 then number becomes odd so, it can't be divisible by 8 so, value of y = 0 ⇒ from the option , we have x = 2,6 ⇒ if x = 2 ,so last 3 digit become = 320 ⇒ 320 is divisible by 8 ⇒ so number = 6278320 ∴ x = 2, y = 0

q_en: If ΔABC is an isosceles triangle with AB = AC and ∠ABC is 65°, then ∠BCA and ∠BAC are, respectively:
e_en: Given: ∠ABC = 65° AB = AC {ΔABC is an isosceles traingle} For mula Used The sum of angle of triangle is 180° Calculation: ⇒ We know that, in isosceles triangle 2 sides and 2 angle are equal ⇒ If AB = AC then ∠ ABC = ∠ACB = 65° ⇒ so, ∠BCA = ∠ACB = 65° ⇒ ∠ABC + ∠ BAC + ∠ACB = 180° ⇒ ∠BAC = 180° - 130° ⇒ ∠BAC = 50°

q_en: The average of the ages of Sonu, Hari and Govind is 30 years. If their ages are in the ratio of 4 : 5: 6 respectively, then the difference between the ages of Sonu and Govind is:
e_en: Given: The average age of Sonu, Hari and Govind = 30 years Formula Used: Average = Sum of observation/No. of observation Calculation: ⇒ Sum of age = 30 × 3 = 90 ⇒ let the age of Sonu, Hari and Govind be 4x, 5x and 6x ⇒ 4x + 5x + 6x = 90 ⇒ 15x = 90 ⇒ x = 6 ⇒ Difference between the ages of Sonu and Govind = 6x - 4x ⇒ 2x = 2 × 6 = 12 years ∴ the difference between the ages of Sonu and Govind is 12 years

q_en: The profit made by selling an article for Rs. 13,400 is equal to the amount of loss incurred on selling the same article at Rs. 11,600. What will be the profit (in Rs.) if it is sold for Rs. 14,750?
e_en: Given: SP₁ = Rs. 13,400 SP₂ = Rs. 11,600 Formula Used: Profit = SP – CP Loss = CP – SP Calculation: Suppose the cost price of the article is CP. According to question – ⇒ 13,400 – CP = CP – 11,600 ⇒ 2CP = 25,000 ⇒ CP = 12,500 If the SP is Rs. 14,750, then, the profit will be = Rs. (14,750 – 12,500) = Rs. 2,250

q_en: The ages of Fatima and Ahmed are in the ratio 3 : 8. The sum of their present ages is 44 years. The difference of their ages is:
e_en: Given: The ages of Fatima and Ahmed are in the ratio 3 : 8. The sum of their present ages is 44 years. Calculation: Suppose the ages of Fatima and Ahmed is 3x and 8x, respectively. According to question – ⇒ 3x + 8x = 44 ⇒ 11x = 44 ⇒ x = 44/11 ⇒ x = 4 Fatima’s age = 3x = 12 years Ahmed’s age = 8x = 32 years Therefore, difference of their ages = (32 – 12) = 20 years

q_en: What sum of money at compound interest will amount to Rs. 4,630.08 in three years if the rate of interest is 4% for the first year, 5% for the second year and 6% for the third year?
e_en: Given: Amount after 3 years = Rs. 4,630.08 Rate of interest for 1, 2 and 3 rd year = 4%, 5% and 6% resp Concept used: Amount = Prinicpal × (1 + r/100)ⁿ Calculation: Amount = Principal × (1 + 4/100) × (1 + 5/100) × (1 + 6/100) Rs. 4,630.08 = Principal × 26/25 × 21/20 × 106/100 Then, Principal = 4,630.08 × 25 × 20 × 100/(26 × 21 × 106) = Rs. 4000 ∴ Principal is Rs. 4000.
